sentences.zh: 三代宮禁之職，《周官》最詳。

translations.literal: The offices of the inner palaces across the Three Dynasties are treated most fully in the Rites of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The duties of the inner palaces in the Three Dynasties are set out most fully in the Rites of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 自周已降，彤史沿革，各載本書，此不備述。

translations.literal: From Zhou downward, the evolution of the inner chronicle is recorded in each book of its own age; this is not set forth in full here.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhou period onward, changes in the inner-palace registers appear in each dynasty's own histories and are not rehearsed here.

sentences.zh: 唐因隋制，皇后之下，有貴妃、淑妃、德妃、賢妃各一人，為夫人，正一品；

translations.literal: Tang followed Sui institutions. Below the empress were one Noble Consort, one Virtuous Consort, one Moral Consort, and one Worthy Consort, styled Ladies, rank one positive;
translations.idiomatic: The Tang adopted Sui practice: beneath the empress stood one each of Noble, Virtuous, Moral, and Worthy Consort, styled Ladies of the first rank;

sentences.zh: 昭儀、昭容、昭媛、修儀、修容、修媛、充儀、充容、充媛各一人，為九嬪，正二品；

translations.literal: Bright Consort, Bright Beauty, Bright Lady, Cultivated Consort, Cultivated Beauty, Cultivated Lady, Fulfilling Consort, Fulfilling Beauty, and Fulfilling Lady — one each — as the Nine Concubines, rank two positive;
translations.idiomatic: the nine posts of Bright, Cultivated, and Fulfilling Consorts, Beauties, and Ladies — one holder each — formed the Nine Concubines of the second rank;

sentences.zh: 婕妤九人，正三品；

translations.literal: nine Fair Ladies, rank three positive;
translations.idiomatic: nine Fair Ladies of the third rank;

sentences.zh: 美人九人，正四品；

translations.literal: nine Beauties, rank four positive;
translations.idiomatic: nine Beauties of the fourth rank;

sentences.zh: 才人九人，正五品；

translations.literal: nine Talented Ladies, rank five positive;
translations.idiomatic: nine Talented Ladies of the fifth rank;

sentences.zh: 寶林二十七人，正六品；

translations.literal: twenty-seven Treasured Forest Ladies, rank six positive;
translations.idiomatic: twenty-seven Treasured Forest Ladies of the sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 御女二十七人，正七品；

translations.literal: twenty-seven Imperial Maidens, rank seven positive;
translations.idiomatic: twenty-seven Imperial Maidens of the seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 采女二十七人，正八品；

translations.literal: twenty-seven Selected Maidens, rank eight positive;
translations.idiomatic: twenty-seven Selected Maidens of the eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 其餘六尚諸司，分典乘輿服御。

translations.literal: The remaining Six Directorates and their offices separately managed the imperial carriage, apparel, and furnishings.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining Six Directorates and their bureaus separately oversaw the imperial equipage, wardrobe, and furnishings.

sentences.zh: ，官名改易，內職皆更舊號。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, titles were changed and all inner offices were given new designations.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo year 2 (656), office titles were revised and every inner-court post was renamed.

sentences.zh: 復舊。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianheng, the former practice was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianheng year 2 (671), the old titles were restored.

sentences.zh: 開元中，玄宗以皇后之下立四妃，法帝嚳也。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, Emperor Xuanzong established four consorts below the empress, following the model of Emperor Ku.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign, Xuanzong placed four consorts beneath the empress, taking Emperor Ku as his precedent.

sentences.zh: 而后妃四星，一為正后；

translations.literal: Yet among the four stars of empress and consorts, one is the principal consort;
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the tradition of the four consort stars, only one is the principal empress;

sentences.zh: 今既立正后，復有四妃，非典法也。

translations.literal: now that a principal consort has been installed, to add four consorts as well is not canonical law.
translations.idiomatic: to install a principal empress and also four consorts is not proper precedent.

sentences.zh: 乃於皇后之下立惠妃、麗妃、華妃等三位，以代三夫人，為正一品；

translations.literal: He therefore established three posts below the empress — Favored Consort, Beautiful Consort, and Splendid Consort — in place of the three Ladies, rank one positive;
translations.idiomatic: He therefore placed Favored, Beautiful, and Splendid Consorts beneath the empress in place of the three Ladies of the first rank;

sentences.zh: 又置芳儀六人，為正二品；

translations.literal: and also appointed six Fragrant Attendants, rank two positive;
translations.idiomatic: and added six Fragrant Attendants of the second rank;

sentences.zh: 美人四人，為正三品；

translations.literal: four Beauties, rank three positive;
translations.idiomatic: four Beauties of the third rank;

sentences.zh: 才人七人，為正四品；

translations.literal: seven Talented Ladies, rank four positive;
translations.idiomatic: seven Talented Ladies of the fourth rank;

sentences.zh: 尚宮、尚儀、尚服各二人，為正五品；

translations.literal: two each for Director of the Palace, Director of Ceremonies, and Director of Apparel, rank five positive;
translations.idiomatic: two each for the Directors of Palace, Ceremonies, and Apparel of the fifth rank;

sentences.zh: 自六品至九品，即諸司諸典職員品第而序之，後亦參用前號。

translations.literal: From rank six through rank nine, the staff of the various offices and bureaus were ordered by grade; later the earlier titles were also used in part.
translations.idiomatic: From the sixth through the ninth rank, posts in the various offices were ranked accordingly, and later the earlier titles were partly revived.

sentences.zh: 然而三代之政，莫不以賢妃開國，嬖寵傾邦。

translations.literal: Yet in the governments of the Three Dynasties, none failed to see worthy consorts help found the state and favored minions overturn it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet across the Three Dynasties, worthy consorts had helped found realms even as favored women brought states to ruin.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢已還，其流浸盛。

translations.literal: From Qin and Han onward, this current grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: From Qin and Han onward, the trend only deepened.

sentences.zh: 大至移國，小則臨朝，煥車服以王宗枝，裂土壤而侯肺腑，洎末塗淪敗，赤族夷宗。

translations.literal: At the greatest they shifted the realm; at the least they held court; they arrayed carriage and robes to ennoble collateral kin, carved out lands to enfeoff in-laws — until, when the end came, whole clans were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: At their worst they moved the throne itself; at their mildest they ruled from behind the curtain — decking kin in state regalia, carving out fiefs for in-laws, until in the final collapse entire clans were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 高祖龍飛，宮無正寢，而婦言是用，釁起維城。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, the palace had no proper principal quarters, yet women's counsel was heeded, and trouble arose among the royal sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, the palace lacked a settled principal consort, yet he heeded women's counsel, and strife broke out among the imperial sons.

sentences.zh: 大帝孝和，仁而不武，但恣池臺之賞，寧顧衽席之嫌？

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong of the Eastern Han was benevolent but not martial; he indulged only in pools and terraces — how could he heed the suspicions of the bedchamber?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong of the Eastern Han was humane but not forceful, lavishing rewards on pools and terraces while ignoring the jealousies of his consorts.

sentences.zh: 武室、韋宗，幾危運祚。

translations.literal: The house of Wu and the clan of Wei nearly endangered the dynasty's fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu and Wei clans nearly brought down the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 東京帝后，歿從夫謚，光烈、和熹之類是也。

translations.literal: Eastern Han empresses, after death, received posthumous titles through their husbands — Guanglie and Hexi are examples.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han empresses took their husbands' posthumous titles after death, as with Guanglie and Hexi.

sentences.zh: 高宗自號天皇，武氏自稱天后，而韋庶人生有翌聖之名，肅宗欲后張氏，此不經之甚，皆以凶終。

translations.literal: Gaozong styled himself Heavenly Emperor and the Wu clan called herself Heavenly Empress; the commoner consort Wei bore the name Sage of the Morrow; Suzong wished to make Lady Zhang empress — these were gross breaches of propriety, and all ended in disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong took the title Heavenly Emperor and Wu Zetian called herself Heavenly Empress; Consort Wei gave birth to a child styled Sage of the Morrow; Suzong wished to elevate Lady Zhang — such gross improprieties all ended in violent ruin.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以惠妃之愛，擯斥椒宮，繼以太真，幾喪天下。

translations.literal: Xuanzong, through love for Favored Consort Wu, pushed aside the pepper chambers, then took Taizhen in succession, and nearly lost the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong, infatuated with Consort Wu, sidelined the principal palace, then elevated Yang Guifei, and nearly lost the empire.

sentences.zh: 歷觀前古邦家喪敗之由，多基於子弟召禍。

translations.literal: Reviewing the causes of ruin in states of old, most rested on sons and younger brothers inviting calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back at fallen dynasties, one finds that ruin usually began with trouble among the emperor's sons.

sentences.zh: 子弟之亂，必始於宮闈不正。

translations.literal: Discord among sons and brothers always begins with disorder in the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Strife among imperial sons always begins with disorder in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 故息隱鬩墻，秦王謀歸東洛；

translations.literal: Thus Suiyuan and Yin fought at the wall, and the Prince of Qin plotted to return to the eastern capital;
translations.idiomatic: Hence the feud between Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji, and the Prince of Qin's plan to withdraw to Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 馬嵬塗地，太子不敢西行。

translations.literal: at Mawei blood soaked the ground, and the crown prince dared not continue west.
translations.idiomatic: at Mawei the road ran with blood, and the crown prince dared not press westward.

sentences.zh: 若中有聖善之慈，胡能若是？

translations.literal: Had there been a mother of holy goodness within, how could things have come to this?
translations.idiomatic: Had a truly virtuous mother presided within, how could matters have reached such a pass?

sentences.zh: 《易》曰「家道正而天下定」，不其然歟！

translations.literal: The Changes says, "When the way of the household is correct, the realm is settled" — is it not so!
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "When the household is in order, the realm is secure" — and so it is!

sentences.zh: 自後累朝，長秋虛位，或以旁宗入繼，母屬皆微，徒有冊拜之文，諒乏「關雎」之德。

translations.literal: In later reigns the seat of the empress often stood empty; sometimes collateral lines succeeded, and the mothers' clans were slight — there were only the words of investiture, but surely lacking the virtue of "Guan Ju."
translations.idiomatic: In later reigns the empress's seat often stood empty; when collateral branches succeeded, the mothers' families were weak — investiture ceremonies remained, but the virtue praised in "Guan Ju" was lacking.

sentences.zh: 今錄其存於史冊者，為《后妃傳》云。

translations.literal: Now those preserved in the historical records are compiled in this Biography of Empresses and Consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Those whose names survive in the histories are recorded here in the Biography of Empresses and Consorts.

sentences.zh: 高祖太穆皇后竇氏高祖太穆皇后竇氏，京兆始平人，隋定州總管、神武公毅之女也。

translations.literal: Empress Taimu of Gaozu, née Dou — Empress Taimu of Gaozu, née Dou, was a native of Shiping in Jingzhao, daughter of Dou Yi, Sui regional inspector of Dingzhou and Duke of Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Taimu of Gaozu, née Dou, came from Shiping in Jingzhao. She was the daughter of Dou Yi, Sui regional inspector of Dingzhou and Duke of Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 后母，周武帝姊襄陽長公主。

translations.literal: Her mother was the Princess of Xiangyang, elder sister of Emperor Wu of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother was the Princess of Xiangyang, a sister of Emperor Wu of the Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 后生而髮垂過頸，三歲與身齊。

translations.literal: At birth her hair hung below her neck; at three it matched her height.
translations.idiomatic: At birth her hair reached below her neck; by age three it matched her height.

sentences.zh: 周武帝特愛重之，養於宮中。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou cherished her especially and raised her in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou doted on her and raised her within the palace.

sentences.zh: 時武帝納突厥女為后，無寵，后尚幼，竊言於帝曰：「四邊未靜，突厥尚強，願舅抑情撫慰，以蒼生為念。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had taken a Turkic woman as empress without favoring her. The girl was still young and whispered to the emperor, "The four borders are not yet calm and the Turks remain strong. I beg my uncle to restrain his feelings and comfort her, keeping the common people in mind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had taken a Turkic woman as empress but showed her no favor. Still a child, the future empress whispered to him, "The borders are unsettled and the Turks remain strong. I beg you, Uncle, to restrain your feelings and treat her kindly for the people's sake.

sentences.zh: 但須突厥之助，則江南、關東不能為患矣。

translations.literal: If only Turkic aid is secured, then the lands south of the Yangtze and east of the Pass cannot become a threat."
translations.idiomatic: With Turkic support secured, the south and the eastern provinces cannot threaten us."

sentences.zh: 」武帝深納之。

translations.literal: "The emperor deeply accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took her counsel to heart.

sentences.zh: 毅聞之，謂長公主曰：「此女才貌如此，不可妄以許人，當為求賢夫。

translations.literal: Yi heard of it and said to the princess, "This girl's talent and beauty are such that she must not be rashly given away; a worthy husband should be sought.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Yi heard of this, he told the princess, "A girl of such talent and beauty must not be given away lightly; we must find a worthy husband for her.

sentences.zh: 」乃於門屏畫二孔雀，諸公子有求婚者，輒與兩箭射之，潛約中目者許之。

translations.literal: "He then painted two peacocks on the door screen. When any young lord came to seek marriage, he was given two arrows to shoot, with a secret agreement that whoever hit the eyes would win her.
translations.idiomatic: He painted two peacocks on the door screen. Each suitor was given two arrows; secretly, whoever struck both eyes would win her hand.

sentences.zh: 前後數十輩莫能中，高祖後至，兩發各中一目。

translations.literal: Several dozen in succession could not hit the mark. Gaozu came last, and with two shots each struck one eye.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of suitors missed the mark. Gaozu came last and with two shots struck one eye each.

sentences.zh: 毅大悅，遂歸於我帝。

translations.literal: Yi was greatly pleased and gave her in marriage to our emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yi was delighted and gave her to our emperor in marriage.

sentences.zh: 及周武帝崩，后追思如喪所生。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou died, she mourned him as though she had lost her own parent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou died, she grieved for him as for her own father.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，后聞而流涕，自投於床曰：「恨我不為男，以救舅氏之難。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, she heard and wept, throwing herself on the bed and saying, "I regret I am not a man, that I might rescue my uncle's plight.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, she wept and threw herself on the bed, crying, "I wish I were a man, that I might save my uncle from this disaster.

sentences.zh: 」毅與長公主遽掩口曰：「汝勿妄言，滅吾族矣！

translations.literal: "Yi and the princess hastily covered her mouth and said, "Do not speak rashly — you will destroy our clan!
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yi and the princess clapped a hand over her mouth: "Do not speak rashly — you will destroy our whole clan!

sentences.zh: 后事元貞太后，以孝聞。

translations.literal: She served Empress Dowager Yuanzhen and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: She served Empress Dowager Yuanzhen and won renown for her filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 太后素有羸疾，時或危篤。

translations.literal: The dowager had long suffered a wasting illness and was sometimes in grave danger.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager had long been frail and sometimes hovered near death.

sentences.zh: 諸姒以太后性嚴懼譴，皆稱疾而退，惟后晝夜扶侍，不脫衣履者，動淹旬月焉。

translations.literal: The other daughters-in-law, fearing the dowager's stern nature and punishment, all pleaded illness and withdrew; only she attended day and night without removing clothes or shoes, often for a full month.
translations.idiomatic: The other daughters-in-law, fearing the dowager's severity, all pleaded illness and withdrew; she alone nursed her day and night without removing shoes or gown, often for a month at a time.

sentences.zh: 善書學，類高祖之書，人不能辯。

translations.literal: She was skilled in calligraphy, resembling Gaozu's hand so that people could not tell them apart.
translations.idiomatic: She wrote beautifully; her hand so resembled Gaozu's that none could tell them apart.

sentences.zh: 工篇章，而好存規戒。

translations.literal: She was accomplished in literary composition and fond of preserving admonitions.
translations.idiomatic: She was accomplished in letters and fond of preserving moral counsel.

sentences.zh: 大業中，高祖為扶風太守，有駿馬數匹。

translations.literal: In the Daye era Gaozu was prefect of Fufeng and owned several fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign Gaozu served as prefect of Fufeng and kept several fine horses.

sentences.zh: 常言於高祖曰：「上好鷹愛馬，公之所知，此堪進御，不可久留，人或言者，必為身累，願熟思之。

translations.literal: She often said to Gaozu, "The emperor loves hawks and horses — you know this. These are fit to present to the throne and must not be kept long. If someone speaks of it, it will surely bring trouble on you. I beg you to consider this carefully.
translations.idiomatic: She often warned Gaozu, "The emperor loves hawks and horses — you know that. These are fit for the throne and must not be kept. If word reaches the court, you will be ruined. Think on this carefully.

sentences.zh: 」高祖未決，竟以此獲譴。

translations.literal: "Gaozu could not decide and in the end was punished for this.
translations.idiomatic: He hesitated, and in the end was punished for keeping them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，后崩於涿郡，時年四十五。

translations.literal: Before long the empress died in Zhuo Commandery at the age of forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward she died in Zhuo Commandery at the age of forty-five.

sentences.zh: 高祖追思后言，方為自安之計，數求鷹犬以進之，俄而擢拜將軍，因流涕謂諸子曰：「我早從汝母之言，居此官久矣。

translations.literal: Gaozu recalled her words and then devised a plan for his own safety, repeatedly seeking hawks and hounds to present; soon he was promoted to general. Weeping, he told his sons, "Had I followed your mother's counsel earlier, I would long since have held this rank.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu recalled her warning and set about securing his position, repeatedly sending hawks and hounds to the throne; soon he was promoted to general. Weeping, he told his sons, "Had I heeded your mother sooner, I would have held this rank long ago.

sentences.zh: 」初葬壽安陵，後祔葬獻陵。

translations.literal: "She was first buried at Shou'an Mausoleum and later removed to share burial at Xian Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: She was first buried at Shou'an Mausoleum and later removed to Xian Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 上元元年八月，改上尊號曰太穆順聖皇后。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Shangyuan, her honorific title was changed to Empress Taimu Shunsheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Shangyuan year 1 (674), her posthumous title was raised to Empress Taimu the Sagely and Accomplished.

sentences.zh: 太宗文德皇后長孫氏太宗文德順聖皇后長孫氏，長安人，隋右驍衛將軍晟之女也。

translations.literal: Empress Wende of Taizong, née Zhangsun — Empress Wende the Sagely and Accomplished of Taizong, née Zhangsun, was a native of Chang'an, daughter of Sui General of the Right Valiant Cavalry Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wende of Taizong, née Zhangsun, came from Chang'an. She was the daughter of Sheng, general of the Right Valiant Cavalry under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 晟妻，隋揚州刺史高敬德女，生后。

translations.literal: Sheng's wife was the daughter of Gao Jingde, Sui inspector of Yangzhou, who bore the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's wife was the daughter of Gao Jingde, Sui inspector of Yangzhou, and bore the empress.

sentences.zh: 少好讀書，造次必循禮則。

translations.literal: From youth she loved reading and in every action followed ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood she loved books and observed propriety in every action.

sentences.zh: 年十三，嬪於太宗。

translations.literal: At thirteen she became a consort of Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen she entered Taizong's household as a consort.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，常歸寧於永興里，后舅高士廉媵張氏，於后所宿舍外見大馬，高二丈，鞍勒皆具，以告士廉。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui she often returned to her family home in Yongxing Lane. Her uncle Gao Shilian's concubine Lady Zhang, outside the quarters where the future empress lodged, saw a great horse two zhang tall with saddle and bridle complete, and reported this to Shilian.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui Daye reign she often visited her family in Yongxing Lane. Her uncle Gao Shilian's concubine Lady Zhang saw outside her quarters a great horse two zhang tall, fully saddled and bridled, and told Shilian.

sentences.zh: 命筮之，遇《坤》之《泰》，筮者曰：「至哉坤元，萬物資生，乃順承天。

translations.literal: He ordered divination and obtained Kun changing to Tai. The diviner said, "How supreme is Kun, source of all things! All beings receive life from it and thereby follow and receive Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He had the omen divined and obtained Kun changing to Tai. The diviner said, "How supreme is the Earth, mother of all things! All life springs from it in obedience to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 坤厚載物，德合無疆。

translations.literal: Kun is thick and bears all things; its virtue joins with boundlessness.
translations.idiomatic: The Earth is vast and bears all things; its virtue knows no limit.

sentences.zh: 牝馬地類，行地無疆。

translations.literal: The mare belongs to the category of earth and moves over the earth without limit.
translations.idiomatic: The mare belongs to the earth and ranges across it without end.

sentences.zh: 變而之《泰》，內陽而外陰，內健而外順，是天地交而萬物通也。

translations.literal: Changing to Tai — yang within and yin without, strength within and compliance without — this is Heaven and Earth in communion and all things in passage.
translations.idiomatic: Changing to Tai — yang within, yin without; strength within, compliance without — Heaven and Earth unite and all things flow freely.

sentences.zh: 《象》曰：后以輔相天地之宜而左右人也。

translations.literal: The Image says: The queen assists in fitting Heaven and Earth to their proper roles and thereby guides the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Image says: The queen assists Heaven and Earth in their proper roles and thereby guides the people.

sentences.zh: 龍，《乾》之象也。

translations.literal: The dragon is the image of Qian.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon is the symbol of Qian.

sentences.zh: 馬，《坤》之象也。

translations.literal: The horse is the image of Kun.
translations.idiomatic: The horse is the symbol of Kun.

sentences.zh: 變而為《泰》，天地交也。

translations.literal: Changing to Tai — Heaven and Earth in communion.
translations.idiomatic: Changing to Tai — Heaven and Earth unite.

sentences.zh: 繇協於《歸妹》，婦人之兆也。

translations.literal: The line text accords with Guimei — an omen for a woman.
translations.idiomatic: The judgment aligns with Marrying the Younger Sister — a woman's omen.

sentences.zh: 女處尊位，履中居順也。

translations.literal: A woman occupying an honored position, treading the center and dwelling in compliance.
translations.idiomatic: A woman in an honored place, centered and compliant in her conduct.

sentences.zh: 此女貴不可言。

translations.literal: This woman's nobility cannot be put into words.
translations.idiomatic: This woman's eminence is beyond words.

sentences.zh: 」武德元年，冊為秦王妃。

translations.literal: "In the first year of Wude she was invested as Princess of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 1 (618) she was invested as Princess of Qin.

sentences.zh: 時太宗功業既高，隱太子猜忌滋甚。

translations.literal: At that time Taizong's achievements were already great and the Hidden Heir's suspicions grew ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: By then Taizong's achievements were great and the crown prince Li Jiancheng's suspicions deepened.

sentences.zh: 后孝事高祖，恭順妃嬪，盡力彌縫，以存內助。

translations.literal: The princess served Gaozu filially, was respectful toward the consorts, and strove to mend relations, preserving support within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: She served Gaozu filially, treated the consorts with respect, and worked to mend palace relations, preserving harmony within.

sentences.zh: 及難作，太宗在玄武門，方引將士入宮授甲，后親慰勉之，左右莫不感激。

translations.literal: When crisis broke out, Taizong was at Xuanwu Gate leading officers into the palace to be armed. She personally comforted and encouraged them; none present was unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: When crisis came, Taizong was at Xuanwu Gate arming his officers. She went out in person to encourage them, and all were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 九年，冊拜皇太子妃。

translations.literal: In the ninth year she was invested as consort of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 (626) she was invested as consort of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, she was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong ascended the throne, she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 贈后父晟司空、齊獻公。

translations.literal: Her father Sheng was posthumously made Minister of Works and Duke of Qixian.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Sheng was posthumously made Minister of Works and Duke of Qixian.

sentences.zh: 后性尤儉約，凡所服御，取給而已。

translations.literal: The empress was especially frugal; whatever she wore or used was only what sufficed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was notably frugal, taking only what she needed for dress and daily use.

sentences.zh: 太宗彌加禮待，常與后論及賞罰之事，對曰：「牝雞之晨，惟家之索。

translations.literal: Taizong treated her with ever greater courtesy and often discussed rewards and punishments with her. She replied, "When the hen crows at dawn, the household is undone.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong treated her with growing respect and often discussed rewards and punishments with her. She replied, "When the hen crows at dawn, the household is ruined.

sentences.zh: 妾以婦人，豈敢豫聞政事？

translations.literal: I am but a woman — how dare I intrude upon state affairs?
translations.idiomatic: I am only a woman — how dare I meddle in government?

sentences.zh: 」太宗固與之言，竟不之答。

translations.literal: "Taizong pressed the matter, but in the end she would not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong pressed her, but she would not reply.

sentences.zh: 時后兄無忌，夙與太宗為布衣之交，又以佐命元勛，委以腹心，出入臥內，將任之朝政。

translations.literal: At that time her elder brother Wuji had long been Taizong's friend in plain clothes and, as a founding merit-holder, was entrusted as a confidant, entering and leaving the sleeping quarters; he was to be placed in charge of court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder brother Zhangsun Wuji had long been Taizong's close friend and, as a founding merit-holder, was trusted as a confidant who entered the inner quarters freely; Taizong meant to place him at the head of government.

sentences.zh: 后固言不可，每乘間奏曰：「妾既托身紫宮，尊貴已極，實不願兄弟子侄布列朝廷。

translations.literal: The empress firmly said this must not be and, seizing every opportunity, memorialized, "Having entrusted myself to the Purple Palace, my honor is already at its height; I truly do not wish brothers, sons, and nephews arrayed through the court.
translations.idiomatic: The empress firmly opposed this and whenever she could said to him, "Having entered the Purple Palace, my honor is already complete; I do not wish my brothers and nephews spread through the court.

sentences.zh: 漢之呂、霍可為切骨之誡，特願聖朝勿以妾兄為宰執。

translations.literal: The Lü and Huo of Han may serve as warnings to the bone; I especially beg the sage court not to make my brother chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Lü and Huo clans of Han are warnings carved in bone; I beg Your Majesty not to make my brother chief minister.

sentences.zh: 」太宗不聽，竟用無忌為左武候大將軍、吏部尚書、右僕射。

translations.literal: "Taizong would not listen and in the end appointed Wuji General of the Left Martial Guard, Minister of Personnel, and Vice Director of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong would not listen and appointed Wuji general of the Left Martial Guard, minister of personnel, and vice director of the left.

sentences.zh: 后又密遣無忌苦求遜職，太宗不獲已而許焉，改授開府儀同三司，后意乃懌。

translations.literal: The empress then secretly sent Wuji to plead earnestly to yield his post. Taizong, unable to refuse, agreed and transferred him to Honorary Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; only then was she content.
translations.idiomatic: She then secretly had Wuji plead to resign. Taizong reluctantly agreed and made him honorary grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon; only then was she satisfied.

sentences.zh: 有異母兄安業，好酒無賴。

translations.literal: She had a half-brother Anye, fond of wine and a wastrel.
translations.idiomatic: She had a half-brother, Anye, a drunkard and wastrel.

sentences.zh: 獻公之薨也，后及無忌並幼，安業斥還舅氏，后殊不以介意，每請太宗厚加恩禮，位至監門將軍。

translations.literal: When Duke Xian died, she and Wuji were both young; Anye drove their mother's clan away. She took no offense and repeatedly asked Taizong to bestow generous favor on him, until he reached the post of gate-guard general.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Xian died, she and Wuji were children; Anye drove away their mother's family. She bore no grudge and repeatedly asked Taizong to treat him generously, until he rose to gate-guard general.

sentences.zh: 及預劉德裕逆謀，太宗將殺之，后叩頭流涕為請命曰：「安業之罪，萬死無赦。

translations.literal: When he became involved in Liu Deyu's treason plot, Taizong was about to execute him. The empress knelt, weeping, and pleaded for his life, saying: "Anye's crime deserves ten thousand deaths and no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: When he became implicated in Liu Deyu's treason plot, Taizong was about to put him to death. The empress knelt, weeping, and pleaded for his life, saying, "Anye's crime deserves death ten thousand times over and admits no pardon.

sentences.zh: 然不慈於妾，天下知之，今置以極刑，人必謂妾恃寵以復其兄，無乃為聖朝累乎！

translations.literal: Yet his lack of kindness toward me is known throughout the realm. If you now impose the extreme penalty, people will surely say I used favor to avenge my brother — would that not burden the sage court!
translations.idiomatic: Yet his lack of kindness toward me is known throughout the realm. If you now impose the death penalty, people will surely say I used my favor to avenge my brother — would that not be a burden on the sacred court!

sentences.zh: 」遂得減死。

translations.literal: "He was spared death.
translations.idiomatic: "He was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 后所生長樂公主，太宗特所鐘愛，及將出降，敕所司資送倍於長公主。

translations.literal: The empress bore Princess Changle, whom Taizong especially cherished. When she was about to marry, he ordered the relevant offices to provide dowry twice that given the elder princesses.
translations.idiomatic: The empress bore Princess Changle, whom Taizong especially cherished. When she was about to marry, he ordered the relevant offices to supply a dowry twice that given to elder princesses.

sentences.zh: 魏徵諫曰：「昔漢明帝時，將封皇子，帝曰：『朕子安得同於先帝子乎！

translations.literal: Wei Zheng remonstrated: "In the time of Emperor Ming of Han, when he was about to enfeoff his sons, the emperor said, 'How can my sons be treated the same as the former emperor's sons!'
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng remonstrated, "In the reign of Emperor Ming of Han, when he was about to enfeoff his sons, the emperor said, 'How can my sons be treated the same as the former emperor's sons!'

sentences.zh: 』然謂長主者，良以尊於公主也，情雖有差，義無等別。

translations.literal: "Yet when one speaks of an elder princess, it is precisely because she ranks above a princess in honor; though affection may differ, the ritual principle admits no equal rank.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet when one speaks of an elder princess, it is precisely because she outranks a princess in honor; though affection may differ, ritual principle admits no equality of rank.

sentences.zh: 若令公主之禮有過長主，理恐不可，願陛下思之。

translations.literal: If the princess's rites exceed those of an elder princess, reason says it cannot stand — I beg Your Majesty to consider this.
translations.idiomatic: If a princess's rites exceed those of an elder princess, reason says it cannot stand — I beg Your Majesty to consider this.

sentences.zh: 」太宗以其言退而告后，后嘆曰：「嘗聞陛下重魏徵，殊未知其故。

translations.literal: "Taizong withdrew on his words and told the empress. She sighed: "I had heard Your Majesty valued Wei Zheng but never knew why.
translations.idiomatic: "Taizong withdrew on his words and told the empress. She sighed, "I had heard Your Majesty valued Wei Zheng but never knew why.

sentences.zh: 今聞其諫，實乃能以義制主之情，可謂正直社稷之臣矣。

translations.literal: Now hearing this remonstrance, I see he can indeed use principle to restrain the lord's feelings — he may truly be called a minister upright for the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I hear this remonstrance, I see he can indeed use principle to restrain the sovereign's feelings — he may truly be called a minister upright for the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 妾與陛下結髮為夫婦，曲蒙禮待，情義深重，每言必候顏色，尚不敢輕犯威嚴，況在臣下，情疏禮隔，故韓非為之說難，東方稱其不易，良有以也。

translations.literal: I and Your Majesty bound our hair as husband and wife and have graciously received your courtesy; our bond runs deep. With every word I still watch your expression and dare not lightly offend your majesty — how much more for subjects below, where feeling is distant and ritual intervenes! Hence Han Fei wrote of the difficulty, and Dongfang Shuo said it was not easy — there was solid reason.
translations.idiomatic: You and I bound our hair as husband and wife, and I have been graciously treated; our bond runs deep. With every word I still watch your expression and dare not lightly offend your majesty — how much more for subjects below, where feeling is distant and ritual stands between! Hence Han Fei wrote of the difficulty, and Dongfang Shuo said it was not easy — and they had good reason.

sentences.zh: 忠言逆於耳而利於行，有國有家者急務，納之則俗寧，杜之則政亂，誠願陛下詳之，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Straight talk grates on the ear yet benefits conduct; rulers of states and households should make it urgent business. Accept it and custom is at peace; shut it out and government falls into disorder. I truly wish Your Majesty to weigh this well — then the realm will be greatly blessed.
translations.idiomatic: Straight talk grates on the ear yet benefits conduct; rulers of states and households should treat it as urgent. Accept it and the realm is at peace; shut it out and government falls into disorder. I truly wish Your Majesty to weigh this carefully — then the realm will be greatly blessed.

sentences.zh: 」后因請遣中使賫帛五百匹，詣徵宅以賜之。

translations.literal: "The empress then asked that an inner envoy be sent bearing five hundred bolts of silk to Wei Zheng's residence as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: "The empress then asked that an inner envoy be sent with five hundred bolts of silk to Wei Zheng's residence as a gift.

sentences.zh: 太子承乾乳母遂安夫人常白后曰：「東宮器用闕少，欲有奏請。

translations.literal: The crown prince Chenggan's wet nurse, Lady Suian, often told the empress: "The Eastern Palace's furnishings are short; I wish to submit a request."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince Chenggan's wet nurse, Lady Suian, often told the empress, "The Eastern Palace's furnishings are in short supply; I wish to submit a request."

sentences.zh: 」后不聽，曰：「為太子，所患德不立而名不揚，何憂少於器物也！

translations.literal: "The empress would not listen and said: "As crown prince, what you should fear is that virtue is not established and your name does not spread abroad — why worry about having too few objects!"
translations.idiomatic: "The empress would not listen and said, "As crown prince, what you should fear is that virtue is not established and your name does not spread — why worry about having too few furnishings!"

sentences.zh: 八年，從幸九成宮，染疾危惙，太子承乾入侍，密啟后曰：「醫藥備盡，尊體不瘳，請奏赦囚徒，並度人入道，冀蒙福助。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when she accompanied him to Jiucheng Palace, she fell gravely ill. Crown Prince Chenggan came to attend her and secretly told the empress: "Medicine has been exhausted; your person does not recover. I beg that amnesty for prisoners be memorialized and persons ordained into the Way, hoping for blessed aid."
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 (634), when she accompanied him to Jiucheng Palace, she fell gravely ill. Crown Prince Chenggan came to attend her and secretly told the empress, "Medicine has been exhausted and you do not recover. I beg that amnesty for prisoners be memorialized and people ordained into the Way, hoping for blessed aid."

sentences.zh: 」后曰：「死生有命，非人力所加。

translations.literal: "The empress said: "Life and death have their allotted span; no human power can add to them.
translations.idiomatic: "The empress said, "Life and death have their allotted span; no human power can alter them.

sentences.zh: 若修福可延，吾素非為惡。

translations.literal: If cultivating merit could extend life, I have never done evil.
translations.idiomatic: If cultivating merit could extend life, I have never done evil.

sentences.zh: 若行善無效，何福可求？

translations.literal: If doing good is without effect, what merit can be sought?
translations.idiomatic: If doing good is without effect, what merit can be sought?

sentences.zh: 赦者，國之大事；

translations.literal: Amnesty is a great matter of state;
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty is a great matter of state;

sentences.zh: 佛道者，示存異方之教耳，非惟政體靡弊，又是上所不為，豈以吾一婦人而亂天下法？

translations.literal: Buddhism and Daoism merely display teachings of other regions — they are not only when government is failing, and moreover they are what the sovereign will not do. How could one woman disorder the laws of the realm?
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism and Daoism merely display teachings from other regions — they are not only for when government is failing, and moreover they are what the sovereign will not do. How could I, one woman, disorder the laws of the realm?

sentences.zh: 」承乾不敢奏，以告左僕射房玄齡，玄齡以聞，太宗及侍臣莫不噓唏。

translations.literal: "Chenggan did not dare memorialize this but told the Left Vice Director Fang Xuanling, who reported it. Taizong and the attending officials all sighed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: "Chenggan did not dare memorialize this but told the left vice director Fang Xuanling, who reported it. Taizong and the attending officials all sighed and wept.

sentences.zh: 朝臣咸請肆赦，太宗從之；

translations.literal: The courtiers all asked for a general amnesty, and Taizong complied;
translations.idiomatic: The courtiers all asked for a general amnesty, and Taizong agreed;

sentences.zh: 后聞之，固爭，乃止。

translations.literal: when the empress heard of it, she firmly opposed it, and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: when the empress heard of it, she firmly opposed it, and the amnesty was stopped.

sentences.zh: 將大漸，與太宗辭訣，時玄齡以譴歸第，后固言：「玄齡事陛下最久，小心謹慎，奇謀秘計，皆所預聞，竟無一言漏泄，非有大故，願勿棄之。

translations.literal: As she was near death, she took leave of Taizong. At that time Xuanling had been sent home under reprimand, and the empress firmly said: "Xuanling has served Your Majesty longest, cautious and careful; his subtle stratagems and secret plans have all been heard by him, yet not a word has leaked — unless there is grave cause, I beg you not to abandon him.
translations.idiomatic: As she was near death, she took leave of Taizong. At that time Xuanling had been sent home under reprimand, and the empress firmly said, "Xuanling has served Your Majesty longest, cautious and careful; his subtle stratagems and secret plans have all been heard by him, yet not a word has leaked — unless there is grave cause, I beg you not to abandon him.

sentences.zh: 又妾之本宗，幸緣姻戚，既非德舉，易履危機，其保全永久，慎勿處之權要，但以外戚奉朝請，則為幸矣。

translations.literal: Also my own clan, fortunate through marriage ties, was raised not for virtue and easily walks into peril; for their lasting preservation, be careful not to place them in positions of power — only let them attend court as maternal kin and that will be enough.
translations.idiomatic: Also my own clan, fortunate through marriage ties, was raised not for virtue and easily walks into peril; for their lasting preservation, be careful not to place them in positions of power — only let them attend court as maternal kin, and that will be enough.

sentences.zh: 妾生既無益於時，今死不可厚費。

translations.literal: I while living was already of no benefit to the age; now in death I must not be richly supplied.
translations.idiomatic: While living I was already of no benefit to the age; now in death I must not be richly supplied.

sentences.zh: 且葬者，藏也，欲人之不見。

translations.literal: Moreover burial means to store away — one wishes that people do not see.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, burial means to store away — one wishes that people do not see.

sentences.zh: 自古聖賢，皆崇儉薄，惟無道之世，大起山陵，勞費天下，為有識者笑。

translations.literal: Since antiquity sage and worthy rulers have all honored thrift; only in lawless ages are great mounds raised, exhausting the realm and becoming a laughingstock to the discerning.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity sage and worthy rulers have all honored thrift; only in lawless ages are great mounds raised, exhausting the realm and becoming a laughingstock to the discerning.

sentences.zh: 但請因山而葬，不須起墳，無用棺槨，所須器服，皆以木瓦，儉薄送終，則是不忘妾也。

translations.literal: Only request burial in the mountains, with no need to raise a mound; do not use inner and outer coffins; whatever vessels and dress are needed, let all be of wood and tile; a thrifty send-off — that is not forgetting me.
translations.idiomatic: Only request burial in the mountains, with no need to raise a mound; do not use inner and outer coffins; whatever vessels and dress are needed, let all be of wood and tile; a thrifty send-off — that is not forgetting me.

sentences.zh: 」十年六月己卯，崩於立政殿，時年三十六。

translations.literal: "On the day jimao of the sixth month of the tenth year she died in Lizheng Hall, aged thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: "On the day jimao of the sixth month of year 10 (636) she died in Lizheng Hall, aged thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月庚寅，葬於昭陵。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin of the eleventh month of that year she was buried at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengyin of the eleventh month of that year she was buried at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 后嘗撰古婦人善事，勒成十卷，名曰《女則》，自為之序。

translations.literal: The empress once compiled good deeds of ancient women, bound into ten scrolls, entitled Regulations for Women, and wrote the preface herself.
translations.idiomatic: The empress once compiled good deeds of ancient women, bound them into ten scrolls entitled Regulations for Women, and wrote the preface herself.

sentences.zh: 又著論駁漢明德馬皇后，以為不能抑退外戚，令其當朝貴盛，乃戒其龍馬水車，此乃開其禍源而防其末事耳。

translations.literal: She also wrote a discourse refuting Empress Ma of Han Mingde, holding that she could not restrain and push back maternal kin, letting them hold noble rank at court — warning them against dragon carriages and water wheels was only to open the source of disaster and guard against the last matter.
translations.idiomatic: She also wrote a discourse refuting Empress Ma of Han Mingde, holding that she could not restrain and push back maternal kin, letting them hold noble rank at court — warning them against dragon carriages and water wheels was only to open the source of disaster and guard against the last matter.

sentences.zh: 且戒主守者曰：「此吾以自防閑耳。

translations.literal: And she warned the keeper of the main seal: "This is for my own guard and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: And she warned the keeper of the main seal, "This is for my own guard and restraint.

sentences.zh: 婦人著述無條貫，不欲至尊見之，慎勿言。

translations.literal: A woman's writings lack orderly scope; I do not wish the Sovereign to see them — do not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: A woman's writings lack orderly scope; I do not wish the Sovereign to see them — do not speak of it.

sentences.zh: 」崩後，宮司以聞，太宗覽而增慟，以示近臣曰：「皇后此書，足可垂於後代。

translations.literal: "After her death the palace office reported it. Taizong read it and his grief deepened; he showed it to his close ministers and said: "The empress's book can indeed be handed down to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: "After her death the palace office reported it. Taizong read it and his grief deepened; he showed it to his close ministers and said, "The empress's book can indeed be handed down to later generations.

sentences.zh: 我豈不達天命而不能割情乎！

translations.literal: Do I not comprehend Heaven's mandate yet cannot cut off affection!
translations.idiomatic: Do I not comprehend Heaven's mandate yet cannot cut off affection!

sentences.zh: 以其每能規諫，補朕之闕，今不復聞善言，是內失一良佐，以此令人哀耳！

translations.literal: Because she could always remonstrate and remedy my deficiencies, I no longer hear good words — this is losing a fine assistant within; that makes one mourn!
translations.idiomatic: Because she could always remonstrate and remedy my deficiencies, I no longer hear good words — this is losing a fine assistant within; that is what makes one mourn!

sentences.zh: 」上元元年八月，改上尊號曰文德順聖皇后。

translations.literal: "In the eighth month of the first year of Shangyuan, her honorific title was changed to Empress Wende the Sagely and Accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: "In the eighth month of Shangyuan year 1 (674), her honorific title was changed to Empress Wende the Sagely and Accomplished.

sentences.zh: 賢妃徐氏太宗賢妃徐氏，名惠，右散騎常侍堅之姑也。

translations.literal: Noble Consort of the Xu clan, favored consort of Taizong — Noble Consort of the Xu clan, favored consort of Taizong, named Hui, niece of the Right Attendant Cavalier-at-Large Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Noble Consort Xu, favored consort of Taizong, named Hui, was a niece of Xu Jian, right attendant cavalier-at-large.

sentences.zh: 生五月而能言，四歲誦《論語》、《毛詩》，八歲好屬文。

translations.literal: At five months she could speak; at four she could recite the Analects and Mao's Odes; at eight she delighted in composition.
translations.idiomatic: At five months she could speak; at four she could recite the Analects and Mao's Odes; at eight she delighted in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 其父孝德試擬《楚辭》，云「山中不可以久留」，詞甚典美。

translations.literal: Her father Xiaode once composed verses in the manner of Songs of Chu, writing "one cannot long remain in the mountains," with wording very classical and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Xiaode once composed verses in the manner of the Songs of Chu, writing "one cannot long remain in the mountains," with wording very classical and beautiful.

sentences.zh: 自此遍涉經史，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: From then on she ranged through the classics and histories, never setting book aside.
translations.idiomatic: From then on she ranged through the classics and histories, never setting a book aside.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞之，納為才人。

translations.literal: When Taizong heard of her, he took her in as a talented lady.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong heard of her, he took her in as a talented lady.

sentences.zh: 其所屬文，揮翰立成，詞華綺贍。

translations.literal: Whatever prose she composed, she finished at the stroke of the brush, her wording ornate and rich.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever prose she composed, she finished at the stroke of the brush, her wording ornate and rich.

sentences.zh: 俄拜婕妤，再遷充容。

translations.literal: Soon she was promoted to Shining Lady, then again to Fulfilling Presence.
translations.idiomatic: Soon she was promoted to Shining Lady, then again to Fulfilling Presence.

sentences.zh: 時軍旅亟動，宮室互興，百姓頗倦勞役，上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: At that time the army marched often and palaces rose one after another; the people grew weary of labor service. She submitted a memorial to remonstrate, saying:
translations.idiomatic: At that time the army marched often and palaces rose one after another; the people grew weary of labor service. She submitted a memorial to remonstrate, saying:

sentences.zh: :「自貞觀已來，二十有二載，風調雨順，年登歲稔，人無水旱之弊，國無饑饉之災。

translations.literal: :"Since the Zhenguan reign, twenty-two years have passed; winds have been temperate and rains timely, the harvest full year after year, the people without harm from flood or drought, the state without famine.
translations.idiomatic: "Since the Zhenguan era, twenty-two years have passed: winds have been temperate and rains timely, harvests full year after year, the people without harm from flood or drought, the state without famine.

sentences.zh: 昔漢武守文之常主，猶登刻玉之符；

translations.literal: Even Emperor Wu of Han, a ruler who kept to the written tradition, still mounted the jade-inscribed tablet;
translations.idiomatic: Even Emperor Wu of Han, a ruler who kept to the written tradition, still mounted the jade-inscribed tablet;

sentences.zh: 齊桓小國之庸君，尚圖泥金之事。

translations.literal: Duke Huan of Qi, a mediocre lord of a small state, still aspired to the clay-and-gold rite.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi, a mediocre lord of a small state, still aspired to the clay-and-gold rite.

sentences.zh: 望陛下推功損己，讓德不居。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will push merit aside and diminish yourself, yielding virtue and not resting in it.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will push merit aside and diminish yourself, yielding virtue and not resting in it.

sentences.zh: 億兆傾心，猶闕告成之禮；

translations.literal: The hundreds of millions bend their hearts, yet the rite of announcing completion is still lacking;
translations.idiomatic: The hundreds of millions bend their hearts, yet the rite of announcing completion is still lacking;

sentences.zh: 雲亭佇謁，未展升中之儀。

translations.literal: At Yun and Ting they wait to attend, yet the ceremony of ascending and offering in the central peak is still not performed.
translations.idiomatic: At Yun and Ting they wait to attend, yet the ceremony of ascending and offering at the central peak is still not performed.

sentences.zh: 此之功德，足以咀嚼百王，網羅千代者矣。

translations.literal: With such merit and virtue, one could chew through the hundred kings and net the thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: With such merit and virtue, one could surpass the hundred kings and encompass the thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 古人有云：「雖休勿休」，良有以也。

translations.literal: The ancients said: "Though at ease, do not rest" — there was solid reason.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, "Though at ease, do not rest" — and they had solid reason.

sentences.zh: 守初保末，聖哲罕兼。

translations.literal: Guarding the beginning and preserving the end — sage and worthy rulers rarely unite both.
translations.idiomatic: Guarding the beginning and preserving the end — sage and worthy rulers rarely unite both.

sentences.zh: 是知業大者易驕，願陛下難之；

translations.literal: Thus we know that when one's enterprise is great, pride comes easily — I hope Your Majesty will find it difficult;
translations.idiomatic: Thus we know that when one's enterprise is great, pride comes easily — I hope Your Majesty will find it difficult;

sentences.zh: 善始者難終，願陛下易之。

translations.literal: when one is good at starting, finishing is hard — I hope Your Majesty will find it easy.
translations.idiomatic: when one is good at starting, finishing is hard — I hope Your Majesty will find it easy.

sentences.zh: :「竊見頃年已來，力役兼總，東有遼海之軍，西有昆丘之役，士馬疲於甲胄，舟車倦於轉輸。

translations.literal: :"I observe that in recent years labor levies have been combined: in the east, armies on the Liaodong sea; in the west, campaigns at Kunqiu Mound. Soldiers and horses weary in armor; boats and carts weary in transport.
translations.idiomatic: "I observe that in recent years labor levies have been combined: in the east, armies on the Liaodong sea; in the west, campaigns at Kunqiu Mound. Soldiers and horses grow weary in armor; boats and carts grow weary in transport.

sentences.zh: 且召募役戍，去留懷死生之痛；

translations.literal: Moreover, recruiting conscripts for garrison duty — going or staying, they bear the pain of life and death;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, recruiting conscripts for garrison duty — whether they go or stay, they bear the pain of life and death;

sentences.zh: 因風阻浪，人米有漂溺之危。

translations.literal: wind and waves intervene — men and grain face the peril of drifting and drowning.
translations.idiomatic: wind and waves intervene — men and grain alike face the peril of drifting and drowning.

sentences.zh: 一夫力耕，卒無數十之獲；

translations.literal: One man's plowing strength harvests at most a few tens;
translations.idiomatic: One man's plowing yields at most a few tens;

sentences.zh: 一船致損，則傾數百之糧。

translations.literal: one ship lost overturns several hundreds' worth of grain.
translations.idiomatic: one ship lost overturns several hundreds' worth of grain.

sentences.zh: 是猶運有盡之農功，填無窮之巨浪，圖未獲之他眾，喪已成之我軍。

translations.literal: This is like transporting finite farming labor to fill endless waves, plotting to gain an enemy not yet won while losing our army already formed.
translations.idiomatic: This is like transporting finite farming labor to fill endless waves, plotting to gain an enemy not yet won while losing our army already formed.

sentences.zh: 雖除凶伐暴，有國常規；

translations.literal: Though eliminating the vicious and punishing the violent are regular duties of a state,
translations.idiomatic: Though eliminating the vicious and punishing the violent are regular duties of a state,

sentences.zh: 然黷武玩兵，先哲所戒。

translations.literal: yet indulging in arms and playing with war are what former sages warned against.
translations.idiomatic: yet indulging in arms and playing with war are what former sages warned against.

sentences.zh: 昔秦皇並吞六國，反速危亡之基；

translations.literal: In the past Qin Shihuang swallowed the six states, yet swiftly laid the foundation for peril and ruin;
translations.idiomatic: In the past Qin Shihuang swallowed the six states, yet swiftly laid the foundation for peril and ruin;

sentences.zh: 晉武奄有三方，翻成覆敗之業。

translations.literal: Jin Wudi embraced three regions, yet turned into the enterprise of overturn and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Wudi embraced three regions, yet turned into the enterprise of overturn and defeat.

sentences.zh: 豈非矜功恃大，棄德而輕邦；

translations.literal: Was it not pride in merit and reliance on greatness, abandoning virtue and slighting the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Was it not pride in merit and reliance on greatness, abandoning virtue and slighting the realm;

sentences.zh: 圖利忘害，肆情而縱欲？

translations.literal: scheming profit and forgetting harm, indulging feeling and giving free rein to desire?
translations.idiomatic: scheming profit and forgetting harm, indulging feeling and giving free rein to desire?

sentences.zh: 遂使悠悠六合，雖廣不救其亡；

translations.literal: Thus the far-reaching six realms, though vast, could not save their ruin;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the far-reaching six realms, though vast, could not save them from ruin;

sentences.zh: 嗷嗷黎庶，因弊以成其禍。

translations.literal: the wailing common people, through exhaustion, were made to complete their disaster.
translations.idiomatic: the wailing common people, through exhaustion, were made to complete their disaster.

sentences.zh: 是知地廣非常安之術，人勞乃易亂之源。

translations.literal: From this one knows that broad territory is not a technique for lasting peace, and human toil is the source of easy disorder.
translations.idiomatic: From this one knows that broad territory is not a technique for lasting peace, and human toil is the source of easy disorder.

sentences.zh: 願陛下布澤流人，矜弊恤乏，減行役之煩，增湛露之惠。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will spread favors and ease the people, pity the weary and succor the needy, reduce the troubles of corvée travel, and increase the grace of generous dew.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will spread favors and ease the people, pity the weary and succor the needy, reduce the troubles of corvée travel, and increase the grace of generous dew.

sentences.zh: 妾又聞為政之本，貴在無為。

translations.literal: Your servant also hears that the root of governing lies in valuing non-action.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant also hears that the root of governing lies in valuing non-action.

sentences.zh: 竊見土木之功，不可兼遂。

translations.literal: I observe that earth-and-timber projects cannot all be completed at once.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that earth-and-timber projects cannot all be completed at once.

sentences.zh: 此闕初建，南營翠微，曾未逾時，玉華創制。

translations.literal: While this palace was first raised, the south was building Cuiwei; before a season had passed, Yuhua was newly founded.
translations.idiomatic: While this palace was first raised, the south was building Cuiwei; before a season had passed, Yuhua was newly founded.

sentences.zh: 雖復因山藉水，非無架築之勞；

translations.literal: Though they followed mountains and borrowed water, it was not without labor of framing and building;
translations.idiomatic: Though they followed mountains and borrowed water, it was not without labor of framing and building;

sentences.zh: 損之又損，頗有工力之費。

translations.literal: diminish again and again — still there was cost in craftsmen's strength.
translations.idiomatic: diminish again and again — still there was cost in craftsmen's strength.

sentences.zh: 終以茅茨示約，猶興木石之疲；

translations.literal: In the end, showing restraint with thatched huts still stirred weariness in wood and stone;
translations.idiomatic: In the end, showing restraint with thatched huts still stirred weariness in wood and stone;

sentences.zh: 假使和雇取人，不無煩擾之弊。

translations.literal: even if hired labor were used, there would not be no trouble of harassment.
translations.idiomatic: even if hired labor were used, there would still be trouble of harassment.

sentences.zh: 是以卑宮菲食，聖主之所安；

translations.literal: Hence low palaces and meager food are what sagely rulers rest in;
translations.idiomatic: Hence low palaces and meager food are what sagely rulers rest in;

sentences.zh: 金屋瑤臺，驕主之為麗。

translations.literal: golden houses and jasper terraces are what arrogant rulers take as splendor.
translations.idiomatic: golden houses and jasper terraces are what arrogant rulers take as splendor.

sentences.zh: 故有道之君，以逸逸人；

translations.literal: Thus rulers who have the Way ease their people;
translations.idiomatic: Thus rulers who have the Way ease their people;

sentences.zh: 無道之君，以樂樂身。

translations.literal: rulers without the Way take joy for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: rulers without the Way take joy for themselves.

sentences.zh: 願陛下使之以時，則力無竭矣；

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will use the people seasonally — then strength will not be exhausted;
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will use the people seasonally — then strength will not be exhausted;

sentences.zh: 用而息之，則人斯悅矣。

translations.literal: use them and let them rest — then the people will be pleased.
translations.idiomatic: use them and let them rest — then the people will be pleased.

sentences.zh: :「夫珍玩伎巧，乃喪國之斧斤；

translations.literal: :"Trinkets, curios, and clever craft are the axes that destroy a state;
translations.idiomatic: "Trinkets, curios, and clever craft are the axes that destroy a state;

sentences.zh: 珠玉錦繡，實迷心之鴆毒。

translations.literal: pearls, jade, brocade, and embroidery are truly the poison that bewilders the heart.
translations.idiomatic: pearls, jade, brocade, and embroidery are truly the poison that bewilders the heart.

sentences.zh: 竊見服玩纖靡，如變化於自然；

translations.literal: I observe dress and play refined to fineness, as if transformed by nature;
translations.idiomatic: I observe dress and play refined to fineness, as if transformed by nature;

sentences.zh: 織貢珍奇，若神仙之所制。

translations.literal: woven tribute of strange wonders, as if made by immortals.
translations.idiomatic: woven tribute of strange wonders, as if made by immortals.

sentences.zh: 雖馳華於季俗，實敗素於淳風。

translations.literal: Though they race with splendor in the fashion of the day, they truly spoil simplicity and ruin pure custom.
translations.idiomatic: Though they race with splendor in the fashion of the day, they truly spoil simplicity and ruin pure custom.

sentences.zh: 是知漆器非延叛之方，桀造之而人叛；

translations.literal: From this one knows lacquer vessels are not a way to postpone rebellion — Jie made them and people rebelled;
translations.idiomatic: From this one knows lacquer vessels are not a way to postpone rebellion — Jie made them and people rebelled;

sentences.zh: 玉杯豈招亡之術，紂用之而國亡。

translations.literal: jade cups are hardly a method to summon ruin — Zhou used them and the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: jade cups are hardly a method to summon ruin — Zhou used them and the state perished.

sentences.zh: 方驗侈麗之源，不可不遏。

translations.literal: One is just verifying that the source of extravagance and beauty must not go unchecked.
translations.idiomatic: One is just verifying that the source of extravagance and beauty must not go unchecked.

sentences.zh: 作法於儉，猶恐其奢；

translations.literal: When one makes policy in thrift, one still fears it will become extravagant;
translations.idiomatic: When one makes policy in thrift, one still fears it will become extravagant;

sentences.zh: 作法於奢，何以制後？

translations.literal: when one makes policy in extravagance, how can one control those who come after?
translations.idiomatic: when one makes policy in extravagance, how can one control those who come after?

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下明鑒未形，智周無際，窮奧秘於麟閣，盡探賾於儒林。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that Your Majesty's bright discernment reaches what is not yet formed, wisdom encircles what has no boundary, exhausts mysteries in the Qilin Pavilion, and thoroughly plumbs the depths in the forest of ru.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant considers that Your Majesty's bright discernment reaches what is not yet formed, wisdom encircles what has no boundary, exhausts mysteries in the Qilin Pavilion, and thoroughly plumbs the depths in the forest of ru.

sentences.zh: 千王治亂之蹤，百代安危之跡，興衰禍福之數，得失成敗之機，故亦苞吞心府之中，循環目圍之內，乃宸衷之久察，無假一二言焉。

translations.literal: The tracks of a thousand kings' order and disorder, the traces of a hundred generations' safety and peril, the numbers of rise and fall with blessing and calamity, the mechanisms of gain and loss with success and failure — thus they are all embraced within the heart's chambers, circling within the scope of the eyes; they are what Your Majesty's inner mind has long scrutinized, with no need for one or two words.
translations.idiomatic: The tracks of a thousand kings' order and disorder, the traces of a hundred generations' safety and peril, the numbers of rise and fall with blessing and calamity, the mechanisms of gain and loss with success and failure — thus they are all embraced within the heart's chambers, circling within the scope of the eyes; they are what Your Majesty's inner mind has long scrutinized, with no need for one or two words.

sentences.zh: 惟恐知之非難，行之不易，志驕於業泰，體逸於時安。

translations.literal: I fear only that knowing what is right is not difficult, but putting it into practice is not easy—that ambition grows proud when undertakings flourish, and the body grows lax when the times are peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: My sole worry is that while recognizing the right path may be easy, walking it is hard: resolve turns arrogant when great works succeed, and discipline slackens when peace lasts too long.

sentences.zh: 伏願抑志裁心，慎終如始，削輕過以添重德，循今是以替前非，則令名與日月無窮，盛業與乾坤永大。

translations.literal: I bow and pray that Your Majesty will restrain ambition and trim the heart, be as careful at the end as at the beginning, pare away light faults to add weighty virtue, and follow the present course to replace past errors—then your fair name will be endless as sun and moon, and your great enterprise as vast as heaven and earth forever.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg you to hold your spirit in check, guard your heart, and treat the finish as you did the start: shed small faults to gain greater virtue, and use the present course to atone for the past. Then your renown will outlast the sun and moon, and your achievements will endure as wide as heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 太宗善其言，優賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Taizong approved of her words and bestowed rich favor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong approved her counsel and rewarded her generously.

sentences.zh: 及太宗崩，追思顧遇之恩，哀慕愈甚，發疾不自醫。

translations.literal: When Taizong died, recalling the grace of his care for her, her mourning grew ever deeper; she fell ill and would not treat herself.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong's death, as she brooded on the kindness he had shown her, her grief deepened; she fell ill and refused medical care.

sentences.zh: 病甚，謂所親曰：「吾荷顧實深，志在早歿，魂其有靈，得侍園寢，吾之志也。

translations.literal: When her illness was severe, she told those close to her: "I have borne deep favor; my wish is an early death; if my soul has spirit, to attend the imperial park-tomb—that is my wish.
translations.idiomatic: As her illness worsened, she told her intimates: "The favor I owe is profound; my heart's wish is to die young. If my spirit lives, to serve in the park-tomb enclosure—that is what I desire.

sentences.zh: 」因為七言詩及連珠以見其志。

translations.literal: " Then she composed a seven-character poem and linked verses to show her intent.
translations.idiomatic: " She then wrote a heptasyllabic poem and a linked-verse piece to express that wish.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年卒，時年二十四，詔贈賢妃，陪葬於昭陵之石室。

translations.literal: She died in the first year of Yonghui, aged twenty-four; an edict posthumously ennobled her as Worthy Consort and buried her in attendance at the stone chamber of Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the first year of Yonghui (650), at twenty-four. An edict granted her posthumously the title Worthy Consort, and she was buried at Zhaoling in its stone chamber.

sentences.zh: 高宗廢后王氏高宗廢后王氏，并州祁人也。

translations.literal: Deposed Empress Wang of Emperor Gaozong—Deposed Empress Wang of Emperor Gaozong—was a native of Qi in Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Empress Wang of Emperor Gaozong—hereafter Deposed Empress Wang of Emperor Gaozong—was from Qi in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父仁祐，貞觀中羅山令。

translations.literal: Her father Renyou was magistrate of Luoshan in the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Ren You served as magistrate of Luoshan during the Zhenguan period.

sentences.zh: 同安長公主，即后之從祖母也。

translations.literal: Princess Chang of Tong'an was the empress's grand-aunt by collateral line.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Chang of Tong'an was her great-aunt.

sentences.zh: 公主以后有美色，言於太宗，遂納為晉王妃。

translations.literal: The princess, because the future empress had beauty, spoke of her to Taizong; she was then taken in as consort to the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Because the future empress was beautiful, the princess spoke of her to Emperor Taizong, and she was given in marriage to the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 高宗登儲，冊為皇太子妃，以父仁祐為陳州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was established as heir, she was invested as crown princess; her father Renyou was made prefect of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong became crown prince, she was named crown princess, and her father Ren You was appointed prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，立為皇后，以仁祐為特進、魏國公，母柳氏為魏國夫人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui she was established as empress; Renyou was made supernumerary grand counsellor and Duke of Wei; her mother the Lady Liu was made Dame of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yonghui she was made empress; Ren You was promoted to supernumerary grand counselor and created Duke of Wei, and her mother Lady Liu was enfeoffed as Dame of Wei.

sentences.zh: 仁祐尋卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: Renyou soon died and was posthumously given the office of Excellency of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Ren You died shortly afterward and was posthumously honored as Grand Counselor of State.

sentences.zh: 初，武皇后貞觀末隨太宗嬪御居於感業寺，后及左右數為之言，高宗由是復召入宮，立為昭儀。

translations.literal: At first, in late Zhenguan, Empress Wu followed Taizong's palace women and dwelt at Ganye Temple; the empress and her attendants repeatedly spoke for her, and Gaozong therefore summoned her back into the palace and established her as Shining Countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the late Zhenguan years, the future Empress Wu had lived at Ganye Temple as one of Taizong's consorts. The empress and her circle spoke for her repeatedly, and Gaozong recalled her to court and made her Shining Countenance.

sentences.zh: 俄而漸承恩寵，遂與后及良娣蕭氏遞相譖毀。

translations.literal: Before long she gradually received favor, and thus she and the empress and the worthy lady Lady Xiao took turns slandering one another.
translations.idiomatic: She soon won the emperor's favor, and she, the empress, and Worthy Lady Xiao traded accusations in turn.

sentences.zh: 帝終不納后言，而昭儀寵遇日厚。

translations.literal: The emperor in the end would not accept the empress's words, while the Shining Countenance's favor grew daily thicker.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would no longer heed the empress, while the Shining Countenance's favor grew stronger day by day.

sentences.zh: 后懼不自安，密與母柳氏求巫祝厭勝。

translations.literal: The empress, fearful and ill at ease, secretly with her mother Lady Liu sought shaman-sorcerers for curse-suppression rites.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful and uneasy, the empress secretly joined her mother Lady Liu in hiring sorcerers for malign rites.

sentences.zh: 事發，帝大怒，斷柳氏不許入宮中，后舅中書令柳奭罷知政事，並將廢后，長孫無忌、褚遂良等固諫，乃止。

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed, the emperor was greatly angry, cut off Lady Liu from entering the inner palace, dismissed the empress's uncle, Grand Counselor Liu Shi, from handling government affairs, and was about to depose the empress; Zhangsun Wuji, Chu Suiliang and others strongly remonstrated, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, the emperor was furious. He barred Lady Liu from the palace, removed the empress's uncle Liu Shi from his post as chief minister, and was on the verge of deposing the empress. Zhangsun Wuji, Chu Suiliang, and others argued fiercely against it, and he relented.

sentences.zh: 俄又納李義府之策，永徽六年十月，廢后及蕭良娣皆為庶人，囚之別院。

translations.literal: Before long he again adopted Li Yifu's plan; in the tenth month of the sixth year of Yonghui the empress and Worthy Lady Xiao were both made commoners and imprisoned in a separate courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took Li Yifu's advice. In the tenth month of the sixth year of Yonghui (655), the empress and Worthy Lady Xiao were reduced to commoners and confined in a separate residence.

sentences.zh: 武昭儀令人皆縊殺之。

translations.literal: The Shining Countenance Wu ordered men to strangle and kill them both.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wu sent men to strangle them.

sentences.zh: 后母柳氏、兄尚衣奉御全信及蕭氏兄弟，並配流嶺外。

translations.literal: The empress's mother Lady Liu, her elder brother Director of Palace Wardrobes Quanxin, and the Xiao brothers were all banished and sent beyond the Ling Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's mother Lady Liu, her brother Quanxin of the Palace Wardrobe, and the Xiao brothers were all exiled beyond the Nanling range.

sentences.zh: 遂立昭儀為皇后。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Shining Countenance was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wu was then enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 尋又追改后姓為蟒氏，蕭良娣為梟氏。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they retroactively changed the empress's surname to Mang ("python") and Worthy Lady Xiao's to Xiao ("owl").
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the deposed empress's clan name was changed to Mang ("python"), and Lady Xiao's to Xiao ("owl-kite").

sentences.zh: 良娣蕭氏庶人良娣初囚，大罵曰：「願阿武為老鼠，吾作貓兒，生生扼其喉！

translations.literal: Worthy Lady Xiao the commoner—when Worthy Lady was first imprisoned she cursed loudly: "May Ah Wu be a mouse and I the cat, strangling its throat life after life!
translations.idiomatic: When Worthy Lady Xiao was first imprisoned as a commoner, she screamed: "May that witch Wu be a mouse and I the cat—I would tear out her throat in every life to come!

sentences.zh: 」武后怒，自是宮中不畜貓。

translations.literal: " Empress Wu was angry; from then on cats were not kept in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: " Wu was furious. From that day the palace kept no cats.

sentences.zh: 初囚，高宗念之，閑行至其所，見其室封閉極密，惟開一竅通食器出入。

translations.literal: When they were first imprisoned, Gaozong missed them and went in leisure to their place; he saw the room sealed extremely tight, with only one opening for food vessels to pass in and out.
translations.idiomatic: Early in their confinement Gaozong still thought of them and strolled to their quarters. The rooms were sealed tight; only a small aperture allowed food to pass through.

sentences.zh: 高宗惻然，呼曰：「皇后、淑妃安在？

translations.literal: Gaozong was moved with pity and called: "Empress, Honored Consort—how are you?
translations.idiomatic: Moved to pity, Gaozong called out: "Empress! Honored Consort! Are you well?

sentences.zh: 」庶人泣而對曰：「妾等得罪，廢棄為宮婢，何得更有尊稱，名為皇后？

translations.literal: " The commoners wept and replied: "We have offended and been cast out as palace maids—how can we still bear honored titles and be called empress?
translations.idiomatic: " They wept and answered: "We are guilty offenders, discarded as palace slaves. How can we still bear the title of empress?

sentences.zh: 」言訖悲咽，又曰：「今至尊思及疇昔，使妾等再見日月，出入院中，望改此院名為『回心院』，妾等再生之幸。

translations.literal: " When they had spoken they sobbed with grief, and again said: "Now Your Majesty thinks on days past and lets us see sun and moon again and go in and out of the courtyard—we beg that this courtyard be renamed 'Courtyard of Turned Hearts'; that would be our fortune of rebirth.
translations.idiomatic: " Their voices broke in grief. They went on: "That Your Majesty remembers the past and lets us see daylight again—if we might walk freely in this courtyard, we beg you rename it the 'Courtyard of the Turning Heart.' That would be rebirth for us.

sentences.zh: 」高宗曰：「朕即有處置。

translations.literal: " Gaozong said: "I shall have arrangements at once.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozong said, "I will see to it.

sentences.zh: 」武后知之，令人杖庶人及蕭氏各一百，截去手足，投於酒甕中，曰：「令此二嫗骨醉！

translations.literal: " When Empress Wu learned of it she had the commoners and Lady Xiao each beaten one hundred strokes with the staff, had hands and feet cut off, and thrown into wine jars, saying: "Let these two crones' bones be drunk!
translations.idiomatic: " When Wu heard, she had each of them flogged a hundred strokes, cut off their hands and feet, and thrown into wine vats, saying, "Let these two hags' bones soak drunk!

sentences.zh: 」數日而卒。

translations.literal: " Within days they died.
translations.idiomatic: " They died within days.

sentences.zh: 後則天頻見王、蕭二庶人披髮瀝血，如死時狀。

translations.literal: Later Wu Zetian frequently saw the two commoners Wang and Xiao with hair loose and dripping blood, as at the time of death.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wu Zetian often saw Wang and Xiao as they had been at death—hair undone, blood streaming.

sentences.zh: 武后惡之，禱以巫祝，又移居蓬萊宮，復見，故多在東都。

translations.literal: Empress Wu hated this; she prayed through shamans and also moved to Penglai Palace, yet still saw them—therefore she was often in the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: She loathed the visions and sought shamans to exorcise them. She moved to Penglai Palace but still saw the ghosts, and thereafter spent much of her time in the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，復后姓為王氏，梟氏還為蕭氏。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, the empress's surname was restored to Wang and the Owl clan returned to Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, the Wang surname was restored and the Xiao clan name as well.

sentences.zh: 中宗和思皇后趙氏中宗和思皇后趙氏，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Empress He-si of Harmonious Thought Zhao of Emperor Zhongzong—Empress He-si of Harmonious Thought Zhao of Emperor Zhongzong—was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Empress He-si ("Harmonious Thought") Zhao of Emperor Zhongzong—hereafter Empress He-si Zhao—was from Chang'an in the capital district.

sentences.zh: 祖綽，武德中以戰功至右領軍衛將軍。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Chuo, by military merit in the Wude era, reached General of the Right Vanguard Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Chuo rose to general of the Right Wing Army on his battlefield record during the Wude years.

sentences.zh: 父瑰，尚高祖女常樂公主，歷遷左千牛將軍。

translations.literal: Her father Gui married Princess Changle, daughter of Gaozu, and rose through posts to General of the Left Palatial Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Gui married Princess Changle, a daughter of Emperor Gaozu, and eventually served as general of the Left Palace Reins Guard.

sentences.zh: 中宗為英王時，納后為妃。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was Prince of Ying, he took the future empress as consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong was Prince of Ying, he made her his princess-consort.

sentences.zh: 既而妃母公主得罪，妃亦坐廢，幽死於內侍省。

translations.literal: Before long the consort's mother the princess offended and was punished; the consort also sat in guilt and was deposed, dying in secret in the Palace Domestic Service Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother the princess fell from favor, the consort was implicated, deposed, and secretly killed in the palace eunuchs' quarters.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，瑰為壽州刺史，坐與越王貞連謀被誅，公主亦坐死。

translations.literal: When Zetian held court, Gui was prefect of Shou; sitting in joint plot with Prince of Yue Zhen, he was executed, and the princess also died by implication.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wu Zetian's regency, Gui was prefect of Shouzhou but was executed for plotting with Prince Zhen of Yue; the princess died as well.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，贈后謚為恭皇后，贈瑰左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong she was posthumously ennobled with the posthumous title Empress Gong ("Respectful") and Gui was given Left Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenlong (705) she was posthumously honored as Empress Gong ("Respectful"), and Gui as commander of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 及中宗崩，將葬於定陵，議者以韋后得罪，不宜祔葬，於是追謚后為和思，莫知瘞所，行招魂祔葬之禮。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong died, as they were about to bury at Dingling, deliberators held that because Empress Wei had offended she should not receive joint burial; thereupon they retroactively gave the empress the posthumous title He-si, but none knew her burial place, and they performed the rite of summoning the soul for joint burial.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongzong's death, as burial at Dingling was planned, court opinion held that the convicted Empress Wei should not be enshrined beside him. The late Empress Zhao was therefore given the posthumous title He-si, but since no one knew where she lay, officials performed a soul-summoning rite for joint burial.

sentences.zh: 太常博士彭景直上言：「古無招魂葬之禮，不可備棺槨，置轀鬻輬。

translations.literal: Libationer Peng Jingzhi of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices submitted: "Antiquity had no rite of burial by summoning the soul; one cannot prepare inner and outer coffins or set out mourning carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Court of Sacrifices academician Peng Jingzhi memorialized: "Antiquity knew no soul-summoning burial. One cannot furnish inner and outer coffins or lay out the full funerary train.

sentences.zh: 宜據《漢書郊祀志》葬黃帝衣冠於橋山故事，以皇后禕衣於陵所寢宮招魂，置衣於魂輿，以太牢告祭，遷衣於寢宮，舒於御榻之右，覆以夷衾而祔葬焉。
