translations.literal: It is fitting to follow the precedent in the Han shu "Treatise on Suburban Sacrifices" of burying the Yellow Emperor's hat and robes at Mount Qiao: with the empress's spirit garment at the spirit couch in the tomb-palace summon the soul, place the garment in the soul carriage, report with the great offering, move the garment to the spirit couch, spread it on the right of the imperial couch, cover with the barbarian-quilt, and thereby perform joint burial.
translations.idiomatic: Follow instead the precedent in the Monograph on Sacrifices in the Book of Han, where the Yellow Emperor's robes were interred at Mount Qiao: bring the empress's spirit robe to the tomb-chamber to summon her soul, place it in the soul carriage, sacrifice with the grand offerings, then lay the robe on the right of the imperial bed, cover it with the funeral pall, and thus complete the joint burial.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " [The court] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The court adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 韋庶人中宗韋庶人，京兆萬年人也。

translations.literal: Commoner consort Wei of Zhongzong—Commoner consort Wei of Zhongzong—was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei of Emperor Zhongzong—hereafter Consort Wei—was from Wannian in the capital district.

sentences.zh: 祖弘表，貞觀中為曹王府典軍。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Hongbiao in Zhenguan served as staff officer of the Prince of Cao's household.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Hongbiao was a staff officer in the household of the Prince of Cao during Zhenguan.

sentences.zh: 中宗為太子時，納后為妃，仍擢后父普州參軍玄貞為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was crown prince he took the future empress as consort, and also promoted her father, militia adjutant Xuanzhen of Pu, to prefect of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhongzong was crown prince he took her as consort and promoted her father Xuanzhen, a militia officer in Pu Prefecture, to prefect of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 嗣聖元年，立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Sisheng she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Sisheng (684) she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 其年，中宗見廢，后隨從房州。

translations.literal: That same year Zhongzong was deposed; the empress followed him to Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Zhongzong was deposed, and the empress accompanied him into exile at Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時中宗懼不自安，每聞制使至，惶恐欲自殺。

translations.literal: At the time Zhongzong feared and was ill at ease; whenever he heard that an imperial emissary had arrived, in panic he wished to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: In those years Zhongzong lived in constant fear. Whenever an imperial envoy was reported, he panicked and was ready to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 后勸王曰：「禍福倚伏，何常之有？

translations.literal: The empress urged the prince: "Calamity and blessing lean on each other—what is ever constant?
translations.idiomatic: The empress comforted him: "Fortune and misfortune turn on each other—what in life is ever fixed?

sentences.zh: 豈失一死，何遽如是也！

translations.literal: How is losing one death worth being so hasty!
translations.idiomatic: Death comes once—why be in such haste to meet it!

sentences.zh: 」累年同艱危，情義甚篤。

translations.literal: " Through many years they shared hardship and peril; their affection was very deep.
translations.idiomatic: " Year after year they shared hardship, and their bond grew very close.

sentences.zh: 所生懿德太子、永泰、永壽、長寧、安樂四公主，安樂最幼，生於房州，帝自脫衣裹之，遂名曰裹兒，特寵異焉。

translations.literal: She bore Crown Prince Yide, and the princesses Yongtai, Yongshou, Changning, and Anle—four princesses; Anle was youngest, born in Fang; the emperor himself stripped off his robe to wrap her, and thus she was named Guo'er ("Bundle-child"), receiving exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Crown Prince Yide and the princesses Yongtai, Yongshou, Changning, and Anle. Anle, the youngest, was born in exile at Fangzhou; the emperor wrapped her in his own robe, hence her nickname "Little Bundle," and she became his especial darling.

sentences.zh: 及中宗復立為太子，又立后為妃。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was again established as crown prince, the empress was again established as consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong was restored as heir apparent, she was again named crown princess.

sentences.zh: 時昭容上官氏常勸后行則天故事，乃上表請天下士庶為出母服喪三年；

translations.literal: At the time Shining Countenance Shangguan often urged the empress to follow Wu Zetian's precedents; she therefore submitted a memorial asking that gentry and commoners observe three years' mourning for a divorced birth-mother;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shangguan, as shining attendant, often urged the empress to follow Wu Zetian's example. She memorialized that all subjects should mourn a divorced birth mother for three full years;

sentences.zh: 又請百姓以年二十三為丁，五十九免役，改易制度，以收時望。

translations.literal: and also asked that the people take year twenty-three as the age of labor service and be exempt at fifty-nine, changing regulations to gather timely esteem.
translations.idiomatic: and that corvée duty should begin at twenty-three and end at fifty-nine—reforms meant to win popular approval.

sentences.zh: 制皆許之。

translations.literal: Edicts all permitted these.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every proposal.

sentences.zh: 帝在房州時，常謂后曰：「一朝見天日，誓不相禁忌。

translations.literal: When the emperor was in Fang he often told the empress: "Once we see heaven and sun again, I vow we shall not restrict each other.
translations.idiomatic: During the Fangzhou exile he often told her: "When we see daylight again, I swear we shall put no restraints on each other.

sentences.zh: 」及得志，受上官昭容邪說，引武三思入宮中，升御床，與后雙陸，帝為點籌，以為歡笑，醜聲日聞於外。

translations.literal: Once he got his wish, accepting the perverse persuasions of Shining Countenance Shangguan, he brought Wu Sansi into the palace; he mounted the imperial couch and played backgammon with the empress while the emperor kept score—they took this for mirth; foul rumors were daily heard outside.
translations.idiomatic: But once restored he heeded the corrupt counsel of Lady Shangguan. He brought Wu Sansi into the palace, where the empress played backgammon with him on the imperial bed while the emperor kept score—all for amusement. Scandalous tales spread daily beyond the walls.

sentences.zh: 乃大出宮女，雖左右內職，亦許時出禁中。

translations.literal: Thereupon he released palace women in large numbers; even attendants of inner posts were allowed to leave the forbidden precincts at times.
translations.idiomatic: He released vast numbers of palace women and even allowed inner attendants to leave the palace grounds from time to time.

sentences.zh: 上官氏及宮人貴幸者，皆立外宅，出入不節，朝官邪佞者候之，恣為狎遊，祈其賞秩，以至要官。

translations.literal: The Shangguan clan and favored palace women all set up outer residences; their comings and goings were unrestrained; flattering court officials waited on them, indulging in intimate outings, praying for rewards and ranks, even to key offices.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shangguan and favored palace women maintained houses outside the palace and came and went without restraint. Sycophantic officials courted them, carousing freely to win favors and promotions, even to the highest posts.

sentences.zh: 時侍中敬暉謀去諸武，武三思患之，乃結上官氏以為援，因得幸於后，潛入宮中謀議，乃諷百官上帝尊號為應天皇帝，后為順天皇后。

translations.literal: At the time Chief Minister Jing Hui plotted to remove the house of Wu; Wu Sansi was troubled by this and therefore allied with the Shangguan clan as aid; thereby he gained favor with the empress, entered the palace in secret for plotting, and prompted the hundred officials to raise the emperor's honorific to "Emperor Responsive to Heaven" and the empress's to "Empress Compliant with Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Jing Hui then sought to purge the Wu clan. Wu Sansi, alarmed, allied with the Shangguans, won access to the empress, and met her secretly in the palace. He prompted the bureaucracy to style the emperor "Emperor Who Responds to Heaven" and the empress "Empress Who Aligns with Heaven."

sentences.zh: 帝與后親謁太廟，告謝受尊號之意。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress personally visited the Imperial Ancestral Temple to report and give thanks for receiving the honorifics.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor and empress went in person to the Imperial Ancestors' Temple to announce and give thanks for the new titles.

sentences.zh: 於是三思驕橫用事，敬暉、王同皎相次夷滅，天下咸歸咎於后。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sansi grew arrogant and wielded power; Jing Hui and Wang Tongjiao were destroyed in succession; all under heaven blamed the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi then ruled arrogantly. Jing Hui and Wang Tongjiao were eliminated in turn, and the realm blamed the empress.

sentences.zh: 后方優寵親屬，內外封拜，遍列清要。

translations.literal: The empress then lavished favor on kin, enfeoffing inside and outside the family, filling every key post.
translations.idiomatic: She showered preferment on her kin, ennobling relatives inside and outside the palace until they filled every important office.

sentences.zh: 又欲寵樹安樂公主，乃制公主開府，置官屬。

translations.literal: She also wished to establish and favor Princess Anle; she therefore decreed that the princess might open a bureau and appoint staff.
translations.idiomatic: She wished to exalt Princess Anle and decreed that the princess might maintain her own bureau with a full staff.

sentences.zh: 太平公主儀比親王。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping's honors matched those of an imperial prince.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping's privileges equaled those of an imperial prince.

sentences.zh: 長寧、安樂二府不置長史而已。

translations.literal: Only the bureaus of Changning and Anle did not appoint chief administrators.
translations.idiomatic: Only the bureaus of Changning and Anle lacked a chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 宜城公主等以非后所生，各減太平之半。

translations.literal: Princesses such as Yicheng, because they were not born of the empress, each had half of Taiping's allotment.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses such as Yicheng, not born to Empress Wei, received half Taiping's allotment.

sentences.zh: 安樂恃寵驕恣，賣官鬻獄，勢傾朝廷，常自草制敕，掩其文而請帝書焉，帝笑而從之，竟不省視。

translations.literal: Anle relied on favor and was arrogant and reckless, selling offices and peddling judgments; her power tilted the court; she often herself drafted edicts, concealed the text and asked the emperor to sign; the emperor smiled and assented, in the end never examining them.
translations.idiomatic: Anle, spoiled and insolent, sold offices and judgments until her power eclipsed the court. She often drafted edicts herself, hid the text, and asked the emperor only to sign. He smiled and agreed without ever reading them.

sentences.zh: 又請自立為皇太女，帝雖不從，亦不加譴。

translations.literal: She also asked to establish herself as heir grand-daughter; though the emperor did not comply, he also did not reprove her.
translations.idiomatic: She even asked to be named heir grand-princess; the emperor refused but did not punish her.

sentences.zh: 所署府僚，皆猥濫非才。

translations.literal: The staff she appointed were all vulgar persons without talent.
translations.idiomatic: The officials she appointed were uniformly unworthy.

sentences.zh: 又廣營第宅，侈靡過甚。

translations.literal: She also widely built mansions, extravagance exceeding all measure.
translations.idiomatic: She built mansions on a lavish scale.

sentences.zh: 長寧及諸公主叠相仿效，天下咸嗟怨之。

translations.literal: Changning and the other princesses piled up imitations of one another; all under heaven sighed and resented them.
translations.idiomatic: Changning and the other princesses vied to imitate her, and public resentment spread across the realm.

sentences.zh: 神龍三年，節湣太子死後，宗楚客率百僚上表，加后號為順天翊聖皇后。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shenlong, after the death of Crown Prince Jiemin, Zong Chuke led the hundred officials in a memorial adding to the empress's title "Empress Compliant with Heaven, Aiding the Sage."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shenlong (707), after Crown Prince Jiemin's death, Zong Chuke led the ministers in memorializing an enhanced title for the empress: "Empress Who Aligns with Heaven and Assists the Sage."

sentences.zh: 景龍二年春，宮中希旨，妄稱后衣箱中有五色雲出，帝使畫工圖之，出示於朝，乃大赦天下，百僚母妻各加邑號。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Jinglong, the palace to please the ruler falsely claimed that five-colored clouds issued from the empress's clothing chest; the emperor had painters depict it and displayed it at court; thereupon he proclaimed a grand amnesty, and every official's mother and wife received enlarged fief titles.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Jinglong (708), courtiers currying favor claimed that five-colored clouds had risen from the empress's wardrobe. The emperor had artists paint the scene and showed it at court, then declared a general amnesty and raised the noble titles of every official's mother and wife.

sentences.zh: 右驍衛將軍、知太史事迦葉誌忠上表曰：

translations.literal: General of the Right Martial Tiger Guard and acting superintendent of the Imperial Astronomical Bureau Yeshi Zhizhong submitted:
translations.idiomatic: General of the Right Martial Tiger Guard and acting director of the Astronomical Bureau Yeshi Zhizhong memorialized:

sentences.zh: :「昔高祖未受命時，天下歌《桃李子》；

translations.literal: "In the past, before Gaozu received the Mandate, the realm sang "Peach and Plum";
translations.idiomatic: "In former times, before Gaozu received the Mandate, the realm sang 'Peach and Plum';

sentences.zh: 太宗未受命時，天下歌《秦王破陣樂》；

translations.literal: before Taizong received the Mandate, the realm sang "Prince of Qin Breaks the Battle Line";
translations.idiomatic: before Taizong received the Mandate, 'Prince of Qin Breaks the Array';

sentences.zh: 高宗未受命時，天下歌《側堂堂》；

translations.literal: before Gaozong received the Mandate, the realm sang "Leaning High and Grand";
translations.idiomatic: before Gaozong received the Mandate, 'Leaning Grand and High';

sentences.zh: 天后未受命時，天下歌《武媚娘》。

translations.literal: before the Heavenly Empress received the Mandate, the realm sang "Lady Wu the Alluring."
translations.idiomatic: before the Celestial Empress received the Mandate, 'Lady Wu the Alluring.'

sentences.zh: 伏惟應天皇帝未受命時，天下歌《英王石州》；

translations.literal: I bow and consider: before the Emperor Responsive to Heaven received the Mandate, the realm sang "Prince of Ying's Stone Prefecture";
translations.idiomatic: Your servant reflects: before the Emperor Who Responds to Heaven received the Mandate, the realm sang 'Prince of Ying's Stonezhou Ballad';

sentences.zh: 順天皇后未受命時，天下歌《桑條韋也》。

translations.literal: before the Empress Compliant with Heaven received the Mandate, the realm sang "Mulberry Branch—Wei Too."
translations.idiomatic: before the Empress Who Aligns with Heaven received the Mandate, 'Mulberry Switch—Wei Too.'

sentences.zh: 女行六合之內，齊首蹀足，應四時八節之會，歌舞同歡。

translations.literal: Women walk within the six directions; they align their heads and stamp their feet, responding to the meetings of the four seasons and eight festivals, singing and dancing in shared joy.
translations.idiomatic: Women across the six directions march in step, stamping together at the four seasons and eight festivals, singing and dancing as one.

sentences.zh: 豈與夫《簫韶》九成、百獸率舞同年而語哉！

translations.literal: How can this be spoken of in the same year as the Ninefold Xiao-shao wherein the hundred beasts lead the dance!
translations.idiomatic: Surely this cannot be mentioned in the same breath as the Ninefold Xiao-shao, when even the beasts led the dance!

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇后降帝女之精，合為國母，主蠶桑以安天下，后妃之德，於斯為盛。

translations.literal: I bow and consider: the empress descends from the essence of an emperor's daughter, unites as mother of the state, presides over sericulture to settle all under heaven—the virtue of empress and consort reaches its height here.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant reflects: the empress embodies the essence of an emperor's daughter, unites the realm as mother of the state, presides over sericulture to settle the world—among consorts her virtue is supreme.

sentences.zh: 謹進《桑條歌》十二篇，伏請宣布中外，進入樂府，皇后先蠶之時，以享宗廟。

translations.literal: I respectfully present twelve sections of the "Mulberry Branch Songs," bowing to request their proclamation inside and outside, entry into the Music Bureau, and that when the empress performs the First Silkworm rite they be used to honor the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully submit twelve stanzas of the 'Mulberry Branch Songs' and beg that they be proclaimed throughout the empire, entered in the Music Bureau, and performed at the empress's First Silkworm ceremony when she offers to the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 帝悅而許之，特賜誌忠莊一區、雜彩七百段。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and permitted it, especially granting Zhizhong one manor-estate and seven hundred lengths of assorted silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and agreed, specially granting Zhizhong an entire estate and seven hundred bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 太常少卿鄭愔又引而申之，播於舞詠，亦受厚賞。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zheng Yin again drew it out and extended it, spreading it in dance-songs; he too received rich reward.
translations.idiomatic: Vice director of the Court of Sacrifices Zheng Yin elaborated the theme in dance-songs and was richly rewarded as well.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書宗楚客又諷補闕趙延禧表陳符命，解《桑條》以為十八代之符，請頒示天下，編諸史冊。

translations.literal: Minister of War Zong Chuke again prompted Remonstrance Archivist Zhao Yanxi to memorialize on portents, interpreting "Mulberry Branch" as the talisman of eighteen generations, requesting proclamation to all under heaven and compilation in the historical annals.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of war Zong Chuke urged remonstrance archivist Zhao Yanxi to memorialize on omens, interpreting 'Mulberry Branch' as the token of eighteen reigns, and asked that it be proclaimed empire-wide and entered in the histories.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，擢延禧為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and promoted Yanxi to Remonstrance Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and promoted Zhao to remonstrance counselor.

sentences.zh: 時上官昭容與其母鄭氏及尚宮柴氏、賀婁氏，樹用親黨，廣納貨賂，別降墨敕，斜封授官，或出臧獲屠販之類，累居榮秩。

translations.literal: At the time Shining Countenance Shangguan with her mother the Lady Zheng and Palace Matrons Chai and Helou planted and used kin cliques, broadly took bribes, separately issued ink edicts, granted offices through slanting seals—some drawn from household slaves, butchers and peddlers—yet piled up in honorific ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shangguan, her mother Lady Zheng, and palace matrons Chai and Helou promoted their kin, took bribes on a vast scale, and issued sealed edicts of their own to sell offices. Slaves, butchers, and peddlers were elevated to honorable rank.

sentences.zh: 又引女巫趙氏出入禁中，封為隴西夫人，勢與上官氏為比。

translations.literal: She also brought in the shamaness Lady Zhao to come and go in the forbidden precincts, enfeoffed her as Dame of Longxi, her power matching the Shangguan clan.
translations.idiomatic: She also admitted the sorceress Lady Zhao into the inner palace, enfeoffed her as Dame of Longxi, and gave her influence equal to the Shangguans.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，帝將親祠南郊，國子祭酒祝欽明、司業郭山惲建議云：「皇后亦合助祭。

translations.literal: In winter of the third year the emperor was about to sacrifice personally at the Southern Suburb; Libationer Zhu Qinming of the Directorate of Education and Vice Director Guo Shanyun proposed: "The empress also should jointly assist at the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year the emperor was to offer sacrifice at the Southern Altar himself. Directorate of Education libationer Zhu Qinming and vice director Guo Shanyun proposed: "The empress should share in the subsidiary rites as well.

sentences.zh: 」太常博士唐紹、蔣欽緒上疏爭之。

translations.literal: " The Masters of Ceremonies at the Temple of Imperial Ancestors Tang Shao and Jiang Qinxu submitted memorials arguing against it.
translations.idiomatic: Masters of Ceremonies Tang Shao and Jiang Qinxu submitted memorials in protest.

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射韋巨源詳定儀注，遂希旨協同欽明之議。

translations.literal: The Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Wei Juyuan worked out the ritual regulations in detail, then to curry favor aligned with Qinming's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Right at the Department of State Affairs Wei Juyuan drafted the ritual code and, eager to please, fell in with Qinming's scheme.

sentences.zh: 帝納其言，以后為亞獻，仍以宰相女為齊娘，以執籩豆。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted their words, made the empress the secondary offerer, and still used prime ministers' daughters as qimei to hold the bian and dou vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took their advice: the empress would serve as secondary offerer, and daughters of chief ministers would be appointed "Imperial maidens" to bear the ritual vessels.

sentences.zh: 欽明又欲請安樂公主為終獻，迫於時議而止。

translations.literal: Qinming again wished to request Princess Anle as final offerer, but was forced by contemporary opinion to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Qinming went further, proposing Princess Anle as final offerer, but public outcry made him abandon the idea.

sentences.zh: 四年正月望夜，帝與后微行市裏，以觀燒燈。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth night of the first month of the fourth year, the emperor and empress went incognito through the marketplace to view the burning lamps.
translations.idiomatic: On the full-moon night of the first month in the fourth year, the emperor and empress slipped out in disguise to wander the streets and watch the lantern festival.

sentences.zh: 又放宮女數千，夜遊縱觀，因與外人陰通，逃逸不還。

translations.literal: He also released several thousand palace women; they roamed by night viewing sights, and because of secret liaisons with outsiders some fled and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: He released several thousand palace women to roam the city at night. Some took illicit lovers among commoners and never came back.

sentences.zh: 時國子祭酒葉靜能善符禁小術，散騎常侍馬秦客頗閑醫藥，光祿少卿楊均以調膳侍奉，皆出入宮掖。

translations.literal: At the time the Directorate libationer Ye Jingneng was skilled in talisman-restraining petty arts; the Attendant-in-Ordinary Ma Qinke was quite versed in medicine and drugs; the Vice Minister of Imperial Entertainments Yang Jun served by adjusting meals—all entered and left the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Libationer Ye Jingneng practiced petty talismanic arts; Attendant-in-Ordinary Ma Qinke knew medicine; Vice Minister Yang Jun managed the imperial kitchen—all passed freely in and out of the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 均與秦客皆得幸於后，相次丁母憂，旬日悉起復舊職。

translations.literal: Both Jun and Qinke gained the empress's favor; each in turn mourned a mother, and within ten days all were recalled to their former posts.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Qinke both won the empress's favor. Each briefly entered mourning for his mother—and within ten days both were back at their posts.

sentences.zh: 時安樂公主與駙馬武延秀、侍中紀處訥、中書令宗楚客、司農卿趙履溫互相猜貳，叠為朋黨。

translations.literal: At the time Princess Anle with her consort Wu Yanxiu, the Attendant-in-Chief Ji Chune, the Grand Counselor Zong Chuke, and the Minister of Imperial Granaries Zhao Lüwen mutually suspected and split off, layering into factions.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anle, her consort Wu Yanxiu, Attendant-in-Chief Ji Chune, Grand Counselor Zong Chuke, and Minister Zhao Lüwen distrusted one another even as they formed rival cliques.

sentences.zh: 六月，帝遇毒暴崩。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the emperor encountered poison and died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the emperor was poisoned and died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 時馬秦客侍疾，議者歸罪於秦客及安樂公主。

translations.literal: At the time Ma Qinke attended his illness; discussants laid blame on Qinke and Princess Anle.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qinke had been at his bedside; rumor soon blamed Qinke and Princess Anle.

sentences.zh: 后懼，秘不發喪，引所親入禁中，謀自安之策。

translations.literal: The empress was afraid, kept secret and did not announce mourning, drew her intimates into the Forbidden Precinct, and plotted strategies to secure herself.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the empress concealed his death and summoned her confidants into the inner palace to plot her own survival.

sentences.zh: 以刑部尚書裴談、工部尚書張錫知政事，留守東都；

translations.literal: She made the Ministers of Punishments Pei Tan and of Works Zhang Xi handle government affairs, to remain guarding the Eastern Capital;
translations.idiomatic: She appointed Pei Tan and Zhang Xi to oversee affairs while she remained at the Eastern Capital;

sentences.zh: 又命左金吾大將軍趙承恩及宦者左監門衛大將軍薛崇簡帥兵五百人往筠州，以備譙王重福。

translations.literal: she also ordered the Left Golden Crow General Zhao Cheng'en and the eunuch Left Gate Guardian General Xue Chongjian to lead five hundred troops to Junzhou to guard against the Prince of Qiao Zhongfu.
translations.idiomatic: and dispatched General Zhao Cheng'en and eunuch general Xue Chongjian with five hundred men to Junzhou to block the Prince of Qiao Zhongfu.

sentences.zh: 后與兄太子少保溫定策，立溫王重茂為皇太子，召諸府兵五萬人屯京城，分為左右營，然後發喪。

translations.literal: The empress with her elder brother the Former Crown Prince Tutor Wen fixed policy, installed the Prince of Wen Chongmao as heir apparent, summoned fifty thousand garrison troops from the various prefectures to camp at the capital, divided into left and right camps, then announced mourning.
translations.idiomatic: She and her brother Wei Wen installed Prince Chongmao as heir apparent, mustered fifty thousand troops in the capital in two camps, and only then announced the emperor's death.

sentences.zh: 少帝即位，尊后為皇太后，臨朝攝政。

translations.literal: The young emperor took the throne, honored the empress as empress dowager, and she attended court to hold regency.
translations.idiomatic: The boy emperor ascended the throne; she became empress dowager and ruled from behind the curtain.

sentences.zh: 韋溫總知內外兵馬，守援宮掖；

translations.literal: Wei Wen overall commanded inner and outer military horses, guarded and supported the palace quarters;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wen commanded all palace and capital forces;

sentences.zh: 駙馬韋捷、韋濯分掌左右屯營；

translations.literal: the consorts-in-law Wei Jie and Wei Zhuo separately held the left and right encampment camps;
translations.idiomatic: his kinsmen by marriage Wei Jie and Wei Zhuo held the left and right camps;

sentences.zh: 武延秀及溫從子播、族弟璿、外甥高崇，共典左右羽林軍及飛騎、萬騎。

translations.literal: Wu Yanxiu and Wen's nephew Bo, clan younger brother Xuan, and nephew-in-law Gao Chong jointly managed the left and right Forest of Feathers Armies and the Flying Cavalry and Ten Thousand Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yanxiu, nephews Bo and Xuan, and Gao Chong controlled the Imperial Guard and the elite cavalry units.

sentences.zh: 播、璿欲先樹威嚴，拜官日先鞭萬騎數人，眾皆怨，不為之用。

translations.literal: Bo and Xuan wished first to establish authority and dignity; on the day of appointment they first flogged several Ten Thousand Cavalry, all resented it and would not serve them.
translations.idiomatic: Bo and Xuan tried to assert authority by flogging guardsmen on their first day in office. The men hated them and refused to fight.

sentences.zh: 時京城恐懼，相傳將有革命之事，往往偶語，人情不安。

translations.literal: At the time the capital was fearful; it was passed about that there would be a dynastic revolution, people often spoke in whispers, and popular sentiment was unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Fear spread through the capital. Whispers of revolution grew; unease ran everywhere.

sentences.zh: 臨淄王率薛崇簡、鐘紹京、劉幽求領萬騎及總監，丁未，入自玄武門，至左羽林軍，斬將軍韋璿、韋播及中郎將高崇於寢帳。

translations.literal: The Prince of Linzi led Xue Chongjian, Zhong Shaojing, and Liu Youqiu commanding the Ten Thousand Cavalry and overseers; on dingwei they entered from the Xuanwu Gate, reached the Left Forest of Feathers Army, and beheaded the Generals Wei Xuan, Wei Bo, and the Captain Gao Chong in the sleeping tent.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day the Prince of Linzi led Xue Chongjian, Zhong Shaojing, and Liu Youqiu with the guard through the Xuanwu Gate into the Left Forest Army camp and cut down Wei Xuan, Wei Bo, and Gao Chong in their quarters.

sentences.zh: 遂斬關而入，至太極殿。

translations.literal: Then they cut the bar and entered, reaching the Hall of Supreme Pole.
translations.idiomatic: They forced the gates and advanced to the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 后惶駭遁入殿前飛騎營，及武延秀、安樂公主皆為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: The empress in terror fled into the Flying Cavalry camp before the hall; along with Wu Yanxiu, Princess Anle were all killed by mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: The empress fled in panic to the Flying Cavalry camp before the hall; mutinous troops killed her, Wu Yanxiu, and Princess Anle.

sentences.zh: 分遣萬騎誅其黨與韋溫、溫從子捷，及族弟嬰；

translations.literal: They separately dispatched the Ten Thousand Cavalry to execute the faction with Wei Wen, Wen's nephew Jie, and the clan younger brother Ying;
translations.idiomatic: Separate detachments hunted down Wei Wen, his nephew Jie, and his clansman Ying;

sentences.zh: 宗楚客、弟晉卿，紀處訥，馬秦客，葉靜能，楊均，趙履溫，衛尉卿王哲，太常卿李，將作少匠李守質及韋氏武氏宗族，無少長皆斬之。

translations.literal: Zong Chuke, younger brother Jinqing, Ji Chune, Ma Qinke, Ye Jingneng, Yang Jun, Zhao Lüwen, the Commandant of Palace Carriages Wang Zhe, the Director of Imperial Sacrifices Li, the Assistant Director of Palace Construction Li Shouzhi, and the Wei and Wu clans—none young or old were spared execution.
translations.idiomatic: together with Zong Chuke, his brother Jinqing, Ji Chune, Ma Qinke, Ye Jingneng, Yang Jun, Zhao Lüwen, Wang Zhe, Li [Director of Sacrifices], Li Shouzhi, and every member of the Wei and Wu lineages, young and old alike. All were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 梟后及安樂公主首於東市。

translations.literal: They exposed the heads of the empress and Princess Anle at the Eastern Market.
translations.idiomatic: Their heads were displayed at the Eastern Market.

sentences.zh: 翌日，敕收后屍，葬以一品之禮，追貶為庶人；

translations.literal: Next day an edict collected the empress's corpse, buried with first-rank rites, posthumously demoted to commoner;
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict ordered her body retrieved and buried with first-rank honors, while posthumously degrading her to commoner status;

sentences.zh: 安樂公主葬以三品之禮，追貶為悖逆庶人。

translations.literal: Princess Anle was buried with third-rank rites, posthumously demoted to Rebellious Commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anle received third-rank burial but was posthumously branded Rebellious Commoner.

sentences.zh: 上官昭容中宗上官昭容，名婉兒，西臺侍郎儀之孫也。

translations.literal: Shangguan Zhaorong of Zhongzong—Shangguan Zhaorong, named Wan'er, was granddaughter of the Vice Director of the Western Terrace Shangguan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Wan'er, styled Zhaorong under Emperor Zhongzong, was granddaughter of Vice Director Shangguan Yi.

sentences.zh: 父庭芝，與儀同被誅，婉兒時在繈褓，隨母配入掖庭。

translations.literal: Her father Tingzhi was executed together with Yi; Wan'er was then in swaddling clothes and followed her mother assigned into the Rear Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Tingzhi was executed with Yi; Wan'er was an infant and entered the palace with her mother.

sentences.zh: 及長，有文詞，明習吏事。

translations.literal: When grown she had literary compositions and clearly understood administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: She grew skilled in letters and well versed in court business.

sentences.zh: 則天時，婉兒忤旨當誅，則天惜其才不殺，但黥其面而已。

translations.literal: In Wu Zetian's time Wan'er offended the decree and should have been executed; Wu Zetian prized her talent and did not kill her, only branded her face.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wu Zetian she once faced execution for an offense; the empress spared her for her talent and only branded her face.

sentences.zh: 自聖歷已後，百司表奏，多令參決。

translations.literal: From the Holy Calendar onward, the hundred offices' memorials and reports she was often made to join in deciding.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shengli era she was regularly consulted on memorials from every department.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，又令專掌制命，深被信任。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne she was again ordered exclusively to hold imperial edicts, deeply trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong put her in charge of drafting edicts and trusted her completely.

sentences.zh: 尋拜為昭容，封其母鄭氏為沛國夫人。

translations.literal: Soon she was appointed Zhaorong; her mother Lady Zheng was enfeoffed Lady of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: She was soon made Zhaorong; her mother Lady Zheng was created Lady of Pei.

sentences.zh: 婉兒既與武三思淫亂，每下制敕，多因事推尊武后而排抑皇家。

translations.literal: Once Wan'er had licentious relations with Wu Sansi, each time edicts were issued she often used the occasion to exalt the Wu and suppress the Imperial House.
translations.idiomatic: After her affair with Wu Sansi, her edicts routinely exalted the Wu clan and slighted the Li imperial house.

sentences.zh: 節湣太子深惡之，及舉兵，至肅章門，扣閣索婉兒。

translations.literal: The Zealous and Stern Crown Prince deeply hated her; when he raised troops and reached the Suozhang Gate he knocked the gate to demand Wan'er.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Chongjun despised her; when he rebelled he hammered at the Suozhang Gate demanding her surrender.

sentences.zh: 婉兒大言曰：「觀其此意，即當次索皇后以及大家。

translations.literal: Wan'er spoke loudly: "Judging by this intent, next they will demand the empress and then His Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Wan'er cried out, "Judging by this, next they will demand the empress—and then Your Majesty himself.

sentences.zh: 」帝與后遂激怒，並將婉兒登玄武門樓以避兵鋒，俄而事定。

translations.literal: " The emperor and empress were thus enraged, and both took Wan'er up the Xuanwu Gate tower to avoid the edge of arms; soon the matter was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress, enraged, escorted her to the Xuanwu Gate tower to escape the fighting. The crisis soon passed.

sentences.zh: 婉兒常勸廣置昭文學士，盛引當朝詞學之臣，數賜遊宴，賦詩唱和。

translations.literal: Wan'er often urged broadly establishing Zhaowen Academicians, lavishly bringing in the dynasty's literary scholars, repeatedly bestowing excursions and banquets, composing poems in call and response.
translations.idiomatic: She urged expanding the Zhaowen Academy, gathering the court's finest writers, and hosting endless banquets of poetry.

sentences.zh: 婉兒每代帝及后、長寧安樂二公主，數首並作，辭甚綺麗，時人咸諷誦之。

translations.literal: Wan'er often substituted for the emperor and empress and the Princesses of Changning and Anle, several pieces composed together; the wording was very ornate, and people of the time all recited them.
translations.idiomatic: She often wrote for the emperor, empress, and the Princesses of Changning and Anle—several poems at once, all of exquisite verse that the age loved to recite.

sentences.zh: 婉兒又通於吏部侍郎崔湜，引知政事。

translations.literal: Wan'er also had relations with the Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Cui Shi and introduced him to know government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: She took Vice Director Cui Shi as lover and secured him a role in government.

sentences.zh: 湜嘗充使開商山新路，功未半而中宗崩，婉兒草遺制，曲敘其功而加褒賞。

translations.literal: Shi once served as envoy to open the new Shangshan road; the work was not half done when Zhongzong died; Wan'er drafted the testamentary edict, bending the narrative of his merit and adding praise and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Shi had been sent to open a new road through Shangshan; the work was unfinished when Zhongzong died. Wan'er drafted the death edict, exaggerating his achievement and heaping rewards upon him.

sentences.zh: 及韋庶人敗，婉兒亦斬於旗下。

translations.literal: When the Commoner of Wei was destroyed, Wan'er too was beheaded beneath the banner.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wei fell, Wan'er was beheaded beneath the rebel standard.

sentences.zh: 玄宗令收其詩筆，撰成文集二十卷，令張說為之序。

translations.literal: Xuanzong ordered collection of her poems and writings, compiled into a twenty-scroll collected works, and had Zhang Yue write its preface.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong gathered her writings into a twenty-scroll collection and had Zhang Yue compose the preface.

sentences.zh: 初，婉兒在孕時，其母夢人遺己大秤，占者曰：「當生貴子，而秉國權衡。

translations.literal: At first when Wan'er was in the womb her mother dreamed someone gave her a great steelyard; the diviner said: "She will bear a noble child and hold the nation's balance-weight.
translations.idiomatic: While Wan'er was in the womb her mother dreamed of receiving a great balance-scale; the diviner said, "You will bear a noble child who will wield the nation's scales.

sentences.zh: 」既生女，聞者嗤其無效，及婉兒專秉內政，果如占者之言。

translations.literal: " When a girl was born listeners mocked its ineffectiveness; when Wan'er exclusively held inner administration it indeed matched the diviner's words.
translations.idiomatic: When a girl was born, all laughed—the prophecy had failed. Yet when Wan'er dominated inner government, the omen proved true.

sentences.zh: 睿宗肅明皇后劉氏睿宗肅明順聖皇后劉氏，刑部尚書德威之孫也。

translations.literal: Empress Suming of Ruizong—Empress Suming Shunsheng of Ruizong, Lady Liu, was granddaughter of the Minister of Punishments Dewei.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Suming Shunsheng, née Liu, consort of Ruizong, was granddaughter of Minister Liu Dewei.

sentences.zh: 父延景，陜州刺史，景雲元年，追贈尚書右僕射、沛國公。

translations.literal: Her father Yanjing was Prefect of Shan; in the first year of Jingyun he was posthumously enfeoffed Right Vice Director and Duke of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Yanjing had been prefect of Shan; in 710 he was posthumously made Right Vice Director and Duke of Pei.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳中，睿宗居籓，納后為孺人，尋立為妃，生寧王憲、壽昌代國二公主。

translations.literal: In Yifeng when Ruizong dwelt on his fief he took her as lady; soon she was established as consort and bore the Prince of Ning Xian and the Princesses of Shouchang and Daiguo.
translations.idiomatic: While Ruizong was a prince in the Yifeng era he took her as consort; she bore Prince Xian of Ning and the Princesses of Shouchang and Daiguo.

sentences.zh: 文明元年睿宗即位，冊為皇后；

translations.literal: In the first year of Civilization Ruizong took the throne and installed her as empress;
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong became emperor in 684 she was made empress;

sentences.zh: 及降為皇嗣，后從降為妃。

translations.literal: when he was reduced to heir-presumptive the empress followed in reduction to consort.
translations.idiomatic: when he was demoted to heir apparent she was reduced to consort.

sentences.zh: 長壽中，與昭成皇后同被譴，為則天所殺。

translations.literal: In Longevity both she and Empress Zhaocheng were punished and sent away, killed by Wu Zetian.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changshou era she and Empress Dou were both condemned and executed by Wu Zetian.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，追謚肅明皇后，招魂葬於東都城南，陵曰惠陵。

translations.literal: First year Jingyun: posthumous title Empress Suming, soul-summoning burial south of the Eastern Capital walls; mausoleum called Huiling.
translations.idiomatic: In 710 she was posthumously titled Empress Suming and given a burial of summoned soul south of Luoyang at Huiling.

sentences.zh: 睿宗崩，遷祔橋陵。

translations.literal: When Ruizong died she was moved for joint burial to Qiaoling.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong died her spirit was moved to share Qiaoling.

sentences.zh: 以昭成太后故，不得入太廟配饗，常別祀於儀坤廟。

translations.literal: Because of Empress Dowager Zhaocheng she could not enter the Grand Temple for shared sacrifice; she was always separately sacrificed at Yikun Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Empress Dowager Dou she was not enshrined in the Grand Ancestral Temple but worshipped separately at Yikun Shrine.

sentences.zh: 開元二十年，始祔太廟。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Kaiyuan she was first jointly enshrined in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In 732 she was at last admitted to the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 昭成皇后竇氏睿宗昭成順聖皇后竇氏，將作大匠抗曾孫也。

translations.literal: Empress Zhaocheng Lady Dou—Ruizong's Empress Zhaocheng Shunsheng Lady Dou—was great-granddaughter of the Master of Palace Construction Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaocheng Shunsheng, née Dou, consort of Ruizong, was great-granddaughter of the master craftsman Dou Kang.

sentences.zh: 祖誕，大理卿、莘國公。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Dan was Grand Justice and Duke of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Dan was Grand Justice and Duke of Shen.

sentences.zh: 父孝諶，潤州刺史，景雲元年，追贈太尉、邠國公。

translations.literal: Her father Xiaochen was Prefect of Run; first year Jingyun posthumously Grand Preceptor and Duke of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Xiaochen had been prefect of Run; in 710 he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Duke of Bin.

sentences.zh: 后姿容婉順，動循禮則，睿宗為相王時為孺人，甚見禮異。

translations.literal: The empress's bearing was gentle and compliant, her movements followed ritual norms; when Ruizong was Prince of Xiang she was a lady and was greatly shown ritual distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and observant of ritual, she won singular honor when Ruizong was Prince of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 光宅元年，立為德妃。

translations.literal: First year Guangye she was established Virtuous Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In 684 she was made Virtuous Consort.

sentences.zh: 生玄宗及金仙、玉真二公主。

translations.literal: She bore Xuanzong and the Princesses Jinxian and Yuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Xuanzong and the Princesses Jinxian and Yuzhen.

sentences.zh: 長壽二年，為戶婢團兒誣譖與肅明皇后厭蠱咒詛。

translations.literal: Second year Longevity she was slandered by the maid Tuan'er that together with Empress Suming she practiced witchcraft pressing and cursing.
translations.idiomatic: In 693 palace maid Tuan'er accused her and Empress Liu of witchcraft and curses.

sentences.zh: 正月二日，朝則天皇后於嘉豫殿，既退而同時遇害。

translations.literal: On the second day of the first month she attended Empress Wu Zetian at the Hall of Abundant Joy; after retiring both were harmed at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the first month they attended Wu Zetian at the Hall of Abundant Joy—and were both slain upon leaving.

sentences.zh: 梓宮秘密，莫知所在。

translations.literal: The inner coffin was secret; none knew its whereabouts.
translations.idiomatic: No one knew where their bodies lay.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，謚曰昭成皇后，招魂葬於都城之南，陵曰靖陵。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne her posthumous title was Empress Zhaocheng, soul-summoning burial south of the capital; mausoleum called Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne he titled her Empress Zhaocheng and gave her a summoned-soul burial south of the capital at Jingling.

sentences.zh: 又立廟於京師，號為儀坤廟。

translations.literal: A temple was also established in the capital called Yikun Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He also founded the Yikun Shrine in the capital.

sentences.zh: 睿宗崩，后以帝母之重，追尊為皇太后，謚仍舊，祔葬橋陵，遷神主於太廟。

translations.literal: When Ruizong died, because of her weight as the emperor's mother she was posthumously honored as empress dowager, posthumous title unchanged, jointly buried at Qiaoling, spirit tablet moved to the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: After Ruizong's death she was honored as empress dowager, reburied at Qiaoling, and her tablet installed in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 玄宗廢后王氏玄宗廢后王氏，同州下邽人，梁冀州刺史神念之後。

translations.literal: Deposed Empress Wang of Xuanzong—Deposed Empress Wang of Xuanzong, native of Xia_gui in Tongzhou, descendant of the Liang Inspector-General Sheinian.
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Empress Wang of Xuanzong, of Xia_gui in Tongzhou, descended from Liang inspector Sheinian.

sentences.zh: 上為臨淄王時，納后為妃。

translations.literal: When the emperor was Prince of Linzi he took her as consort.
translations.idiomatic: He married her when he was Prince of Linzi.

sentences.zh: 上將起事，頗預密謀，贊成大業。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to raise the affair he took part in secret plotting and assisted in accomplishing the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: She took part in the secret plotting of his coup and helped bring it to success.

sentences.zh: 先天元年，為皇后，以父仁皎為太僕卿，累加開府儀同三司、邠國公。

translations.literal: First year Xiantian she became empress; her father Renjiao was made Grand Stablemaster, cumulatively added Kaifu yitong sansi, Duke of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: In 712 she became empress; her father Renjiao rose to Grand Stablemaster, then Kaifu yitong sansi, then Duke of Bin.

sentences.zh: 后兄守一以后無子，常懼有廢立，導以符厭之事。

translations.literal: The empress's elder brother Shouyi because the empress had no son constantly feared removal or installation, and guided her with talisman and pressing matters.
translations.idiomatic: Her brother Shouyi, fearing her childlessness would cost her the throne, led her into talismanic sorcery.

sentences.zh: 有左道僧明悟為祭南北斗，刻霹靂木，書天地字及上諱，合而佩之，且祝曰：「佩此有子，當與則天皇后為比。

translations.literal: There was an unorthodox-way monk Mingwu who sacrificed to the Southern and Northern Dippers, carved thunderbolt wood, wrote Heaven-and-Earth characters and the emperor's taboo, joined and wore it, and moreover prayed: "Wearing this brings sons; she shall be compared with Empress Wu Zetian.
translations.idiomatic: The heterodox monk Mingwu sacrificed to the Dippers, carved thunder-wood talismans inscribed with heaven-and-earth characters and the emperor's name, and prayed: "Who wears this shall bear a son and match Empress Wu.

sentences.zh: 」事發，上親究之，皆驗。

translations.literal: " When the affair broke out the emperor personally investigated; all was verified.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed the emperor investigated personally—and every charge proved true.

sentences.zh: 開元十二年秋七月己卯，下制曰：「皇后王氏，天命不祐，華而不實。

translations.literal: Twelfth year Kaiyuan autumn seventh month jimao, an edict was issued: "Empress Wang—Heaven's mandate does not bless her; flowering yet without fruit.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day in the seventh month of 724 an edict declared: "Empress Wang lacks Heaven's favor—splendid appearance, hollow substance.

sentences.zh: 造起獄訟，朋扇朝廷，見無將之心，有可諱之惡。

translations.literal: She created and raised lawsuits, formed factions fanning the court; shown was a heart without submission, deplorable evils that may be tabooed.
translations.idiomatic: She stirred lawsuits and faction in court, showed a rebellious heart, and committed unspeakable crimes.

sentences.zh: 焉得敬承宗廟，母儀天下？

translations.literal: How could she reverently receive the ancestral temples and mother the realm?
translations.idiomatic: How could she tend the ancestral shrines or mother the realm?

sentences.zh: 可廢為庶人，別院安置。

translations.literal: She may be deposed as commoner and lodged in a separate courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Depose her to commoner rank and house her in a separate palace.

sentences.zh: 刑於家室，有愧昔王，為國大計，蓋非獲已。

translations.literal: Punishment in the family chamber—she owes guilt to kings of old; for the state's great plan it is surely not obtained willingly.
translations.idiomatic: Family discipline shames the ancient kings; for the state's sake the throne acts with deepest reluctance.

sentences.zh: 」守一賜死。

translations.literal: " Shouyi was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，庶人卒，以一品禮葬於無相寺。

translations.literal: That year tenth month the commoner died, buried with first-rank rites at Wuxiang Temple.
translations.idiomatic: She died that October and was buried with first-rank honors at Wuxiang Temple.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，雪免，復尊為皇后。

translations.literal: First year Baoying her stigma was cleared, again honored as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In 762 her conviction was cleared and she was restored as empress.

sentences.zh: 貞順皇后武氏玄宗貞順皇后武氏，則天從父兄子恆安王攸止女也。

translations.literal: Empress Zhenshun Lady Wu—Xuanzong's Empress Zhenshun Lady Wu—was daughter of Wu Zetian's father's elder brother's son the Prince of Heng'an Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhenshun, née Wu, consort of Xuanzong, was daughter of Prince Youzhi of Heng'an, Wu Zetian's clansman.

sentences.zh: 攸止卒後，后尚幼，隨例入宮。

translations.literal: After Youzhi died the future empress was still young and by precedent entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: After Youzhi's death she was still a child and entered the palace by custom.

sentences.zh: 上即位，漸承恩寵。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne she gradually received favor and doting.
translations.idiomatic: After his accession she gradually won his favor.

sentences.zh: 及王庶人廢後，特賜號為惠妃，宮中禮秩，一同皇后。

translations.literal: When the Commoner Wang was deposed as empress she was specially granted the title Exalted Consort; within the palace ritual rank was identical to the empress.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Wang's fall she was titled Exalted Consort (Huifei), with ritual standing equal to the empress.

sentences.zh: 所生母楊氏，封為鄭國夫人。

translations.literal: Her birth mother Lady Yang was enfeoffed Lady of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother Lady Yang was created Lady of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 同母弟忠，累遷國子祭酒；

translations.literal: Same-mother younger brother Zhong was repeatedly promoted to Directorate libationer;
translations.idiomatic: Her half-brother Zhong rose to libationer of the Directorate of Education;

sentences.zh: 信，秘書監。

translations.literal: Xin was Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: her half-brother Xin became Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 惠妃開元初產夏悼王及懷哀王、上仙公主，並繈褓不育，上特垂傷悼。

translations.literal: Early Kaiyuan Huifei bore the Prince of Summer Mourning, the Prince of Cherished Lament, and the Princess of Upper Immortal—all in swaddling did not live; the emperor especially bent in grief and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan she bore three children who died in infancy; the emperor mourned each deeply.

sentences.zh: 及生壽王瑁，不敢養於宮中，命寧王憲於外養之。

translations.literal: When she bore the Prince of Longevity Mao he dared not rear him in the palace and ordered the Prince of Ning Xian to rear him outside.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Shou (Mao) was born he dared not raise him in the palace and had Prince of Ning Xian rear him outside.

sentences.zh: 又生盛王琦，咸宜、太華二公主。

translations.literal: She also bore the Prince of Sheng Qi and the Princesses Xianyi and Taihua.
translations.idiomatic: She later bore Prince Qi of Sheng and the Princesses Xianyi and Taihua.

sentences.zh: 惠妃以開元二十五年十二月薨，年四十餘。

translations.literal: Huifei in the twelfth month of the twenty-fifth year Kaiyuan passed away, age forty-some.
translations.idiomatic: Huifei died in the twelfth month of 737, aged over forty.

sentences.zh: 下制曰：「存有懿範，沒有寵章，豈獨被於朝班，故乃施於亞政，可以垂裕，斯為通典。

translations.literal: An edict said: "While living there is fine model; after death there is favor's charter—not alone bestowed on the court ranks, thus applied to secondary governance; it can hand down abundance—this is the universal canon.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "The living deserve exemplary virtue; the dead honor in title—not for courtiers alone but for those who shaped inner governance—such is enduring custom.

sentences.zh: 故惠妃武氏，少而婉順，長而賢明，行合禮經，言應圖史。

translations.literal: Thus Huifei Lady Wu: young and gentle, grown and worthy and bright; conduct accorded with the ritual classics, words responded to the chart-histories.
translations.idiomatic: Exalted Consort Wu was gentle in youth and wise in maturity; her conduct matched the classics, her words the chronicles.

sentences.zh: 承戚里之華胄，升後庭之峻秩，貴而不恃，謙而益光。

translations.literal: She bore the splendid lineage of the affinal kin quarter, ascended the lofty rank of the rear court; noble yet not relying on it, modest and thereby more radiant.
translations.idiomatic: Born to imperial kin, she rose to the palace's highest rank—proud rank yet not arrogant, modesty only increasing her luster.

sentences.zh: 以道飭躬，以和逮下，四德粲其兼備，六宮咨而是則。

translations.literal: With the Way she disciplined her person, with harmony she reached those below; the four virtues shone together complete, the six palaces consulted and took her as standard.
translations.idiomatic: She governed herself by the Way, harmonized those beneath her, embodied all four virtues, and set the standard for the six palaces.

sentences.zh: 法度在己，靡資珩佩；

translations.literal: Standards and measure were in her own person, not relying on pendant gems;
translations.idiomatic: She upheld propriety through her own conduct, not through the ornaments of rank;

sentences.zh: 躬儉化人，率先絺纮。

translations.literal: Personally frugal she transformed others, taking the lead in coarse hemp.
translations.idiomatic: Her personal austerity set the example, leading others even to wear plain hemp.

sentences.zh: 夙有奇表，將加正位，前後固讓，辭而不受，奄至淪歿，載深感悼，遂使玉衣之慶，不及於生前；

translations.literal: Long she had a remarkable bearing; [the emperor] was about to confer the principal position; before and after she firmly declined, declining and not accepting; suddenly she reached extinction and demise; [he] deeply grieved and mourned; thus causing the jade-garment celebration, not to reach while living;
translations.idiomatic: Of singular grace, she was to be elevated to chief consort, yet repeatedly declined the honor. When she died suddenly, the emperor's grief was profound: the rites of the jade garment never crowned her in life;

sentences.zh: 象服之榮，徒增於身後。

translations.literal: the glory of elephant garb, vainly increased after her person.
translations.idiomatic: only the posthumous honors of her rank remained to exalt her memory.

sentences.zh: 可贈貞順皇后，宜令所司擇日冊命。

translations.literal: May be posthumously granted Empress Zhenshun; it is fitting to order the relevant offices to choose a day for investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Let her be posthumously styled Empress Zhenshun, with the proper offices to choose a day for the enshrinement rites.

sentences.zh: 」葬於敬陵。

translations.literal: " She was buried at Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried at Jingling."

sentences.zh: 時慶王琮等請制齊衰之服，有司請以忌日廢務，上皆不許之。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Qing Cong and others requested to order full mourning garments; the responsible offices requested to suspend duties on the anniversary day; the emperor all did not permit them.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Qing and others asked to wear full mourning for her; officials proposed suspending court business on her death anniversary—the emperor refused both.

sentences.zh: 立廟於京中昊天觀南，乾元之後，祠享亦絕。

translations.literal: A temple was erected south of Haotian Abbey in the capital; after Qianyuan, sacrifices and offerings also ceased.
translations.idiomatic: A shrine was built south of Haotian Abbey in Chang'an; after the Qianyuan era (758–760), even memorial offerings ceased.

sentences.zh: 楊貴妃玄宗楊貴妃，高祖令本，金州刺史。

translations.literal: Consort Yang—Xuanzong's Consort Yang: Ancestor Lingben, Governor of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yang, favorite of Emperor Xuanzong: her ancestor Yang Lingben had served as governor of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 父玄琰，蜀州司戶。

translations.literal: Her father Xuanyan, Registrar of Shu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Yang Xuanyan was registrar of Shu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 妃早孤，養於叔父河南府士曹玄璬。

translations.literal: The consort was orphaned early and was reared by her uncle, the Henan Circuit registrar Xuanjiong.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, she was raised by her uncle Xuanjiong, a registrar in the Henan prefectural government.

sentences.zh: 開元初，武惠妃特承寵遇，故王皇后廢黜。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyuan, Consort Wu Huifei especially received favor and grace; therefore Empress Wang was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan reign, Consort Wu Huifei enjoyed exceptional favor, and Empress Wang was deposed.

sentences.zh: 二十四年惠妃薨，帝悼惜久之，後庭數千，無可意者。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Huifei passed away; the emperor mourned and cherished her long; the rear court numbered thousands, none pleasing to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huifei died in 736, the emperor mourned her for a long while; among the thousands in the inner palace, none could please him.

sentences.zh: 或奏玄琰女姿色冠代，宜蒙召見。

translations.literal: Someone memorialized that Xuanyan's daughter's beauty crowned the age and that she ought to receive summons and audience.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Xuanyan's daughter was the most beautiful woman of the age and ought to be summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 時妃衣道士服，號曰太真。

translations.literal: At the time the consort wore Taoist robes and was styled Taizhen.
translations.idiomatic: At the time she wore Taoist robes and was known as Taizhen.

sentences.zh: 既進見，玄宗大悅。

translations.literal: Once she had been presented in audience, Xuanzong was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: After she was presented, Xuanzong was delighted.

sentences.zh: 不期歲，禮遇如惠妃。

translations.literal: Within less than a year, courtesies and treatment were like those for Huifei.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year she received honors equal to those once granted Huifei.

sentences.zh: 太真姿質豐艷，善歌舞，通音律，智算過人。

translations.literal: Taizhen's figure and substance were lush and resplendent; she was skilled at song and dance, understood musical pitch and mode, and her wit and calculation surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhen was voluptuous and radiant, skilled in song and dance, versed in music, and sharper in mind than most.

sentences.zh: 每倩盼承迎，動移上意。

translations.literal: Each time with coquettish glances she attended and welcomed him, she moved and swayed the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Her every glance and gesture swayed the emperor's mood.

sentences.zh: 宮中呼為「娘子」，禮數實同皇后。

translations.literal: Within the palace she was called "Niangzi"; ritual propriety was in fact the same as for the empress.
translations.idiomatic: The palace called her "My Lady," and in ceremony she was treated virtually as empress.

sentences.zh: 有姊三人，皆有才貌，玄宗並封國夫人之號：長曰大姨，封韓國；

translations.literal: She had three elder sisters, all possessing talent and beauty; Xuanzong together enfeoffed them with the title State Lady: the eldest was called the Great Aunt and enfeoffed as Lady of Han;
translations.idiomatic: She had three sisters, all gifted and beautiful; Xuanzong ennobled them as State Ladies: the eldest, called Big Aunt, became Lady of Han;

sentences.zh: 三姨，封虢國；

translations.literal: the Third Aunt, enfeoffed as Lady of Guo;
translations.idiomatic: the third sister as Lady of Guo;

sentences.zh: 八姨，封秦國。

translations.literal: the Eighth Aunt, enfeoffed as Lady of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: and the eighth sister as Lady of Qin.

sentences.zh: 並承恩澤，出入宮掖，勢傾天下。

translations.literal: All received grace and favor, entering and leaving the palace quarters; their power tilted the realm.
translations.idiomatic: They all shared her favor, moved freely in and out of the palace, and their influence dominated the empire.

sentences.zh: 妃父玄琰，累贈太尉、齊國公；

translations.literal: The consort's father Xuanyan was repeatedly posthumously granted Grand Commandant and Duke of Qi;
translations.idiomatic: Her father Xuanyan was posthumously promoted to Grand Commandant and Duke of Qi;

sentences.zh: 母封涼國夫人；

translations.literal: her mother was enfeoffed as Lady of Liang;
translations.idiomatic: her mother was styled Lady of Liang;

sentences.zh: 叔玄珪，光祿卿。

translations.literal: her uncle Xuangui, Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: her uncle Xuangui became Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 再從兄銛，鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: Her second cousin Xian, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Her cousin Xian was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 锜，侍御史，尚武惠妃女太華公主，以母愛，禮遇過於諸公主，賜甲第，連於宮禁。

translations.literal: Qi, Palace Censor, married Huifei's daughter Princess Taihua; because of his mother's love, courtesies exceeded those for the other princesses; he was granted a great mansion connected to the palace precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, a palace censor, married Princess Taihua, daughter of Huifei; through his mother's favor he outranked other imperial sons-in-law and received a grand residence adjoining the palace walls.

sentences.zh: 韓、虢、秦三夫人與銛、锜等五家，每有請托，府縣承迎，峻如詔敕，四方賂遺，其門如市。

translations.literal: The three Ladies of Han, Guo, and Qin together with Xian, Qi, and the other five households—whenever they had requests and commissions, prefectures and counties received and welcomed them as sternly as if imperial edicts; bribes and gifts from the four directions, their gates like a market.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the three State Ladies and the five Yang households made a request, local officials obeyed as if it were an edict; gifts poured in from every quarter until their gates resembled a marketplace.

sentences.zh: 皇場五載七月，貴妃以微譴送歸楊銛宅。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year of the reign, the Noble Consort because of a slight reproof was sent back to Yang Xian's residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Kaiyuan 5 (717), the consort was briefly banished to Yang Xian's house for a minor offense.

sentences.zh: 比至亭午，上思之，不食。

translations.literal: By the time it reached midday, the emperor thought of her and did not eat.
translations.idiomatic: By noon the emperor was pining for her and would not eat.

sentences.zh: 高力士探知上旨，請送貴妃院供帳、器玩、廩餼等辦具百餘車，上又分御饌以送之。

translations.literal: Gao Lishi probed and learned the emperor's intent and requested to send to the consort's quarters bedding, utensils and playthings, grain provisions and the like—over a hundred cartloads of furnishings; the emperor again divided his imperial viands to send to her.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lishi, sensing the emperor's mood, sent more than a hundred cartloads of bedding, furnishings, and provisions to her quarters, and the emperor shared his own meals with her.

sentences.zh: 帝動不稱旨，暴怒笞撻左右。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor was stirred and things did not accord with his intent, he flew into rage and flogged those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The slightest displeasure sent him into a rage, and he beat his attendants.

sentences.zh: 力士伏奏請迎貴妃歸院。

translations.literal: Lishi, prostrate, memorialized requesting to welcome the Noble Consort back to her quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi knelt and asked permission to bring the consort back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 是夜，開安興里門入內，妃伏地謝罪，上歡然慰撫。

translations.literal: That night the Anxing Lane gate was opened for her to enter within; the consort prostrated herself to confess guilt; the emperor gladly comforted and soothed her.
translations.idiomatic: That night the Anxing Lane gate opened to admit her; she prostrated herself in apology, and the emperor received her with joy.

sentences.zh: 翌日，韓、虢進食，上作樂終日，左右暴有賜與。

translations.literal: The next day the Ladies of Han and Guo presented food; the emperor made music all day; those at his side suddenly received gifts and grants.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Ladies of Han and Guo sent delicacies; music played all day, and attendants received sudden largesse.

sentences.zh: 自是寵遇愈隆。

translations.literal: From this time favor and treatment grew ever more lofty.
translations.idiomatic: From then on her favor only deepened.

sentences.zh: 韓、虢、秦三夫人歲給錢千貫，為脂粉之資。

translations.literal: The three Ladies of Han, Guo, and Qin each year were granted a thousand strings of cash as funds for rouge and powder.
translations.idiomatic: The three State Ladies received a thousand strings of cash yearly for cosmetics.

sentences.zh: 銛授三品、上柱國，私第立戟。

translations.literal: Xian was granted third rank and Pillar of the State; at his private residence halberds were erected.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was made a third-rank Pillar of the State, with ceremonial halberds set before his mansion.

sentences.zh: 姊妹昆仲五家，甲第洞開，僭擬宮掖，車馬僕禦，照耀京邑，遞相誇尚。

translations.literal: The five households of sisters and brothers-in-law had mansions gaping open, presumptuously imitating the palace quarters; chariots, horses, servants and outriders illuminated the capital; they in turn vaunted and admired one another.
translations.idiomatic: The five Yang households built mansions rivaling the palace itself; their carriages and retinues blazed through the capital as each strove to outshine the others.

sentences.zh: 每構一堂，費逾千萬計，見制度宏壯於己者，即撤而復造，土木之工，不舍晝夜。

translations.literal: Whenever they built one hall, the expense exceeded ten million in reckoning; when they saw a structure grander than their own, they at once demolished and rebuilt; earth and timber work did not cease day or night.
translations.idiomatic: Each hall cost more than ten million cash; if they saw a finer building elsewhere, they tore theirs down and rebuilt, with construction crews laboring day and night.

sentences.zh: 玄宗頒賜及四方獻遺，五家如一，中使不絕。

translations.literal: What Xuanzong bestowed and granted and what the four directions presented as gifts—the five households were treated as one; palace envoys never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial gifts and tribute from every region were divided equally among the five households, with palace envoys arriving without pause.

sentences.zh: 開元已來，豪貴雄盛，無如楊氏之比也。

translations.literal: Since Kaiyuan began, among the powerful and noble in heroic splendor, none compared to the Yang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Kaiyuan era began, no clan had matched the Yang in wealth and power.

sentences.zh: 玄宗凡有遊幸，貴妃無不隨侍，乘馬則高力士執轡授鞭。

translations.literal: Whenever Xuanzong had excursions and visits, the Noble Consort never failed to attend and serve; when riding a horse, Gao Lishi held the reins and handed the whip.
translations.idiomatic: On every imperial outing the consort accompanied him; when she rode, Gao Lishi held her reins and offered her whip.

sentences.zh: 宮中供貴妃院織錦刺繡之工，凡七百人，其雕刻熔造，又數百人。

translations.literal: Within the palace those supplying the Noble Consort's quarters for brocade weaving and embroidery numbered seven hundred in all; for carving, casting and smelting, again several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Seven hundred artisans in the palace wove brocades and embroidery for her quarters; several hundred more did carving and metalwork.

sentences.zh: 揚、益、嶺表刺史，必求良工造作奇器異服，以奉貴妃獻賀，因致擢居顯位。

translations.literal: Governors of Yang, Yi, and Lingnan circuits invariably sought skilled craftsmen to make strange vessels and unusual garments to present to the Noble Consort as congratulatory offerings, and thereby were promoted to lofty positions.
translations.idiomatic: Governors of Yangzhou, Yizhou, and the far south vied to commission exotic goods as gifts to the consort, and many were promoted for it.

sentences.zh: 玄宗每年十月幸華清宮，國忠姊妹五家扈從，每家為一隊，著一色衣，五家合隊，照映如百花之煥發，而遺鈿墜舄，瑟瑟珠翠，燦爛芳馥於路。

translations.literal: Each year in the tenth month Xuanzong visited Huaqing Palace; Guozhong and the sisters' five households followed in attendance; each household formed one company, wearing one color of garment; the five households combined their companies, reflecting and shining like a hundred flowers bursting forth; lost hairpins and fallen shoes, sèsè jade beads and kingfisher inlay, brilliant and fragrant along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Each October Xuanzong visited Huaqing Palace with Guozhong and the five Yang households in train. Each family marched in a single color; together they bloomed like a garden in procession, shedding hairpins, shoes, pearls, and kingfisher ornaments that scented the road.

sentences.zh: 而國忠私於虢國而不避雄狐之刺，每入朝或聯鑣方駕，不施帷幔。

translations.literal: Yet Guozhong was intimate with the Lady of Guo and did not avoid the male fox's sting; whenever he entered court or sometimes yoked chariots side by side, they did not hang curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong carried on an affair with the Lady of Guo with scandalous openness; they sometimes rode paired chariots to court without even drawing curtains.

sentences.zh: 每三朝慶賀，五鼓待漏，艷妝盈巷，蠟炬如晝。

translations.literal: At each thrice-monthly celebration and congratulation, at the fifth watch they awaited the clepsydra drip; splendid makeup filled the lanes; wax torches were like daytime.
translations.idiomatic: At the thrice-monthly court celebrations they arrived before dawn in full regalia, filling the streets with torchlight bright as day.

sentences.zh: 而十宅諸王百孫院婚嫁，皆因韓、虢為紹介，仍先納賂千貫而奏請，罔不稱旨。

translations.literal: As for the Ten Residences princes and the Hundred Grandsons Academy marriages, all went through Han and Guo as go-betweens; they still first paid bribes of a thousand strings before memorializing requests—none failed to accord with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Marriages among the imperial clansmen in the Ten Residences and Hundred Grandsons Academy all passed through the Ladies of Han and Guo as brokers; a thousand strings of cash secured each petition, and none was refused.

sentences.zh: 天寶九載，貴妃復忤旨，送歸外第。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianbao, the Noble Consort again offended the imperial intent and was sent back to the outer residence.
translations.idiomatic: In 750 the consort again offended the emperor and was sent to her family's house.

sentences.zh: 時吉溫與中貴人善，溫入奏曰：「婦人智識不遠，有忤聖情，然貴妃久承恩顧，何惜宮中一席之地，使其就戮，安忍取辱於外哉！

translations.literal: At the time Ji Wen was on good terms with the inner eunuch favorites; Wen entered and memorialized, saying: "Women's wisdom and knowledge do not reach far; there was offense to the sage feeling, yet the Noble Consort long received grace and regard—why begrudge one place within the palace? To make her go to execution—how bear to take disgrace outside!"
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wen, who was close to the chief eunuchs, memorialized: "Women lack foresight and may offend Your Majesty, yet the consort has long enjoyed your favor. Why deny her a place in the palace? To let her face death abroad—how could you bear such shame for her!"

sentences.zh: 」上即令中使張韜光賜御饌，妃附韜光泣奏曰：「妾忤聖顏，罪當萬死。

translations.literal: " The emperor at once ordered the palace envoy Zhang Taoguang to bestow imperial viands; the consort, appended to Taoguang, weeping memorialized, saying: "Your handmaid offended the sage countenance; guilt deserves ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the eunuch Zhang Taoguang with imperial food. The consort, weeping, sent word through him: "I have offended Your Majesty and deserve death.

sentences.zh: 衣服之外，皆聖恩所賜，無可遺留，然髮膚是父母所有。

translations.literal: Apart from clothing, all were gifts of sage grace, nothing to leave behind; yet hair and skin are what parents possessed.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from these garments, all I own is your gift and I can leave nothing behind—yet my hair and skin were given by my parents.

sentences.zh: 」乃引刀翦髮一繚附獻。

translations.literal: " Thereupon she drew a knife, cut a lock of hair, attached it and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: She cut a lock of her hair and sent it with her message.

sentences.zh: 玄宗見之驚惋，即使力士召還。

translations.literal: Xuanzong, seeing it, was startled and grieved; he at once ordered Lishi to summon her back.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong was stricken with remorse and ordered Lishi to bring her back at once.

sentences.zh: 國忠既居宰執，兼領劍南節度，勢漸恣橫。

translations.literal: Once Guozhong occupied the chancellorship and concurrently held the Jiannan command, his power gradually grew reckless and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guozhong became chief minister and also held the Jiannan command, his power grew insolent.

sentences.zh: 十載正月望夜，楊家五宅夜遊，與廣平公主騎從爭西市門。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth-night moon of the first month of the tenth year, the Yang clan's five mansions made a night excursion and contended at the West Market gate with the Princess of Guangping's mounted followers.
translations.idiomatic: On the Lantern Night of the first month in 751, the five Yang households rode out and clashed at the West Market gate with Princess Guangping's escort.

sentences.zh: 楊氏奴揮鞭及公主衣，公主墮馬，駙馬程昌裔扶主，因及數撾。

translations.literal: A Yang household slave swung a whip and struck the princess's garment; the princess fell from her horse; the consort's husband Cheng Changyi supported his mistress and thereby received several blows as well.
translations.idiomatic: A Yang servant's whip struck the princess's robe; she fell from her horse. Her husband Cheng Changyi helped her up and was beaten several times himself.

sentences.zh: 公主泣奏之，上令殺楊氏奴，昌裔亦停官。

translations.literal: The princess, weeping, memorialized it; the emperor ordered the Yang slave killed; Changyi also had his office suspended.
translations.idiomatic: The princess wept and reported the affair; the emperor ordered the Yang servant executed and stripped Changyi of his post.

sentences.zh: 國忠二男昢、暄，妃弟鑒，皆尚公主，楊氏一門尚二公主、二郡主。

translations.literal: Guozhong's two sons Can and Xuan, the consort's younger brother Jian—all married princesses; the Yang clan in one gate married two princesses and two commandery princesses.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong's sons Can and Xuan and the consort's brother Jian all married imperial women; the Yang clan thus wed two princesses and two commandery princesses.

sentences.zh: 貴妃父祖立私廟，玄宗御制家廟碑文並書。

translations.literal: The Noble Consort's father and grandfather established a private ancestral temple; Xuanzong personally composed the family temple stele text and also wrote it.
translations.idiomatic: A private ancestral temple was built for her forebears; Xuanzong composed and personally inscribed its stele.

sentences.zh: 玄珪累遷至兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Xuangui was repeatedly transferred up to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangui rose to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，范陽節度使安祿山大立邊功，上深寵之。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao period, Fanyang Military Commissioner An Lushan greatly established frontier merit; the emperor deeply favored him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era, An Lushan, military commissioner of Fanyang, won great victories on the frontier and earned the emperor's deep favor.

sentences.zh: 祿山來朝，帝令貴妃姊妹與祿山結為兄弟。

translations.literal: When Lushan came to court, the emperor ordered the Noble Consort's sisters and Lushan to form a bond as brothers.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan came to court, the emperor had the consort's sisters and Lushan swear brotherhood.

sentences.zh: 祿山母事貴妃，每宴賜，錫賚稠沓。

translations.literal: Lushan treated the consort as mother; at each banquet and grant, gifts and bestowals were thick and piled.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan addressed the consort as his mother; at every feast the emperor showered him with gifts.

sentences.zh: 及祿山叛，露檄數國忠之罪。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, he issued an open proclamation enumerating Guozhong's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled, his public manifesto listed Guozhong's crimes.

sentences.zh: 河北盜起，玄宗以皇太子為天下兵馬元帥，監撫軍國事。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Hebei; Xuanzong made the Crown Prince commander-in-chief of all armies and horses under heaven to oversee and comfort military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: With rebellion spreading in Hebei, Xuanzong named the crown prince commander of all forces to oversee military affairs.

sentences.zh: 國忠大懼，諸楊聚哭，貴妃銜土陳請，帝遂不行內禪。

translations.literal: Guozhong was greatly afraid; the various Yangs gathered and wept; the Noble Consort held earth in her mouth and memorialized in plea; the emperor then did not carry out inner abdication.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong was terrified; the Yang clan wept together while the consort begged on bended knee, and the emperor abandoned the planned abdication.

sentences.zh: 及潼關失守，從幸至馬嵬，禁軍大將陳玄禮密啟太子，誅國忠父子。

translations.literal: When Tong Pass was lost and [the emperor] followed in flight to Mawei, the Imperial Guard general Chen Xuanli secretly informed the Crown Prince and executed Guozhong father and sons.
translations.idiomatic: After Tong Pass fell, the court fled to Mawei, where Imperial Guard general Chen Xuanli secretly urged the crown prince to execute Guozhong and his sons.

sentences.zh: 既而四軍不散，玄宗遣力士宣問，對曰「賊本尚在」，蓋指貴妃也。

translations.literal: Soon after the four armies did not disperse; Xuanzong sent Lishi to proclaim and inquire; they replied, "The rebels' root is still present"—this referred to the Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: The troops still would not disperse. Xuanzong sent Lishi to ask their grievance; they answered, "The root of the rebellion remains"—meaning the consort.

sentences.zh: 力士復奏，帝不獲已，與妃詔，遂縊死於佛室。

translations.literal: Lishi again memorialized; the emperor, unable to obtain his wish, issued an edict to the consort; she was then strangled to death in the Buddha hall.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi reported again; the emperor, left no choice, gave the order, and she was strangled in a chapel.

sentences.zh: 時年三十八，瘞於驛西道側。

translations.literal: At the time she was thirty-eight; she was buried beside the road west of the post station.
translations.idiomatic: She was thirty-eight; her body was buried beside the post road.

sentences.zh: 上皇自蜀還，令中使祭奠，詔令改葬。

translations.literal: When the Retired Emperor returned from Shu, he ordered palace envoys to offer sacrifices and decreed reburial.
translations.idiomatic: After the retired emperor returned from Shu, he sent eunuchs to offer sacrifices and ordered her reburial.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎李揆曰：「龍武將士誅國忠，以其負國兆亂。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Li Kui said: "The Longwu guardsmen executed Guozhong because he betrayed the state and foreboded chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Li Kui said: "The Longwu guards killed Guozhong for betraying the state and bringing on rebellion.

sentences.zh: 今改葬故妃，恐將士疑懼，葬禮未可行。

translations.literal: Now to rebury the former consort— I fear the guardsmen will suspect and dread; the burial rites cannot yet be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: To rebury the former consort now may alarm the troops; the funeral cannot proceed."

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " Thereupon it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was halted.

sentences.zh: 上皇密令中使改葬於他所。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor secretly ordered palace envoys to rebury her at another place.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor secretly ordered eunuchs to rebury her elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 初瘞時以紫褥裹之，肌膚已壞，而香囊仍在。

translations.literal: At the first burial she was wrapped in a purple coverlet; flesh and skin had already decayed, yet the fragrant pouch still remained.
translations.idiomatic: At the first burial she had been wrapped in a purple quilt; though her flesh had decayed, her perfumed sachet remained intact.

sentences.zh: 內官以獻，上皇視之淒惋，乃令圖其形於別殿，朝夕視之。

translations.literal: Inner officials presented it; the Retired Emperor, viewing it, was desolate and grieved; he then ordered her likeness painted in a separate hall and viewed morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuchs presented it, the retired emperor wept in grief and had her portrait painted in a side hall, which he gazed upon morning and night.

sentences.zh: 馬嵬之誅國忠也，虢國夫人聞難作，奔馬至陳倉。

translations.literal: At Mawei, when Guozhong was executed, the Lady of Guo, hearing trouble arise, spurred her horse and fled to Chencang.
translations.idiomatic: When Guozhong was killed at Mawei, the Lady of Guo fled on horseback toward Chencang.

sentences.zh: 縣令薛景仙率人吏追之，走入竹林。

translations.literal: Magistrate Xue Jingxian led clerks and attendants in pursuit; she ran into a bamboo grove.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Xue Jingxian pursued her with his officers into a bamboo grove.

sentences.zh: 先殺其男裴徽及一女。

translations.literal: First they killed her son Pei Hui and one daughter.
translations.idiomatic: They killed her son Pei Hui and a daughter first.

sentences.zh: 國忠妻裴柔曰：「娘子為我盡命。

translations.literal: Guozhong's wife Pei Rou said: "Niangzi, for my sake exhaust your life.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong's wife Pei Rou said, "My lady, end my life for me.

sentences.zh: 」即刺殺之。

translations.literal: " She at once stabbed and killed her.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Guo stabbed her dead.

sentences.zh: 已而自刎，不死，縣吏載之，閉於獄中。

translations.literal: Afterward she cut her own throat; she did not die; county clerks loaded her and confined her in prison.
translations.idiomatic: She then tried to cut her own throat but survived; the officers took her to jail.

sentences.zh: 猶謂吏曰：「國家乎？

translations.literal: She still said to the clerks: "The state?
translations.idiomatic: She still asked the jailer, "Are you the state?

sentences.zh: 賊乎？

translations.literal: Rebels?
translations.idiomatic: Or rebels?"

sentences.zh: 」吏曰：「互有之。

translations.literal: " The clerk said: "Each has some.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "A bit of both."

sentences.zh: 」血凝至喉而卒，遂瘞於郭外。

translations.literal: " Blood congealed to her throat and she expired; she was then buried outside the outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: Blood clogged her throat and she died; they buried her outside the city wall.

sentences.zh: 韓國夫人婿秘書少監崔峋，女為代宗妃。

translations.literal: The Lady of Han's son-in-law, Vice Director of the Secretariat Cui Xun—his daughter was a consort of Emperor Daizong.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Han's son-in-law Cui Xun, vice director of the Secretariat, had a daughter who became a consort of Emperor Daizong.

sentences.zh: 虢國男裴徽尚代宗女延安公主，女嫁讓帝男。

translations.literal: The Lady of Guo's son Pei Hui married Emperor Daizong's daughter Princess Yan'an; a daughter married a son of the Emperor who Abdicated.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Guo's son Pei Hui had married Princess Yan'an, daughter of Daizong; a daughter married a son of the retired emperor.

sentences.zh: 秦國夫人婿柳澄先死，男鈞尚長清縣主，澄弟潭尚肅宗女和政公主。

translations.literal: The Lady of Qin's son-in-law Liu Cheng died first; the son Jun married the Princess of Changqing Commandery; Cheng's younger brother Tan married Emperor Suzong's daughter Princess Hezheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Qin's son-in-law Liu Cheng died early; her son Jun married a commandery princess of Changqing, and Cheng's brother Tan married Princess Hezheng, daughter of Suzong.
